title: Stories worth telling / حكايات تستحق أن تُروى

outcome.canDo: I can tell a connected story about a personal turning point, using narrative tenses and clear sequencing.
outcome.canDoArabic: أستطيع أن أحكي قصة متصلة عن نقطة تحول شخصية باستخدام أزمنة السرد وإشارات التتابع بوضوح.
outcome.scenario: You need to explain a personal turning point to a friend and say what happened, how you felt, and what changed as a result — giving a clear sequence of events and a short evaluation.
outcome.scenarioArabic: تحتاج إلى شرح نقطة تحول شخصية لصديق: ماذا حدث، كيف شعرت، وما الذي تغيّر نتيجة لذلك — مع تقديم تسلسل واضح للأحداث وتقييم قصير.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Write 3–4 sentences about one important experience from last year: say what happened, how you felt, and one change that followed. Use past tenses.
retrieval.purpose: Repurpose A2 'experiences' into a B1 connected mini-narrative that prepares you for longer storytelling.

retrieval.language: Arabic
retrieval.prompt: اكتب ثلاث جمل عن خطة (plan) فعلتها ولم تسر كما توقعت. اذكر ماذا خططت، ماذا فعلت، وكيف تغيّرت خطتك.
retrieval.purpose: يحَوِّل فِكرة A2 'خطط' إلى مهمة سردية قصيرة تتعامل مع التغيير والحل العملي.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Say in 2–3 sentences whether you prefer telling stories face-to-face or writing them down, and give one reason.
retrieval.purpose: Uses A2 'preferences' to prompt a qualified opinion with justification — practise linking opinion to personal experience.

retrieval.language: Arabic
retrieval.prompt: صف خدمة (service) تلقيتها — مثل إصلاح أو رعاية طبية — واذكر خطوات المشكلة والحل بإيجاز.
retrieval.purpose: يحوّل موضوع A2 'الخدمات' إلى سرد عملي عن مشكلة وحل، مع تسلسل أحداث واضح.

network.anchor: Tell the story: what happened, when, how you felt, and what changed afterwards.
priorLevelLinks: A2: describing plans and simple past events
A2: describing services or simple problems
A2: language for change (past and future)
network.learningNote: Focus on narrative tenses (past simple, past continuous, past perfect) and sequencing words (when, while, after, before, by the time, eventually). Teach multi-word chunks useful for storytelling and practise organising a beginning, middle and end.
network.learningNoteArabic: التركيز على أزمنة السرد (الماضي البسيط، الماضي المستمر، الماضي التام) وكلمات التسلسل (عندما، بينما، بعد أن، قبل أن، بحلول الوقت، في النهاية). تدريس عبارات متعددة الكلمات المفيدة للسرد والتدرّب على تنظيم البداية والوسط والنهاية.

wordFamilies.note: Use 'remember' and 'recall' for bringing a memory to mind; 'remembrance' is a noun often used in formal contexts.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: استخدم 'remember' و'recall' لاسترجاع الذاكرة؛ 'remembrance' اسم يُستخدم غالبًا في سياقات رسمية.

wordFamilies.note: 'decision' is the noun; 'decisive' describes someone who makes choices quickly and firmly.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: 'decision' اسم؛ 'decisive' صفة لوصف شخص يتخذ قرارات بسرعة وبحزم.

wordFamilies.note: Talk about 'change' as a process (changing) and results (changed).
wordFamilies.noteArabic: تحدث عن 'change' كعملية (changing) ونتائج (changed).

vocabulary.definition: an important moment when a situation changes significantly
vocabulary.exampleEN: Leaving home for university was a turning point in my life.
vocabulary.exampleAR: الذهاب إلى الجامعة كان نقطة تحول في حياتي.

vocabulary.definition: a clear, detailed recollection of an event
vocabulary.exampleEN: I have a vivid memory of the smell of the kitchen at my grandparents' house.
vocabulary.exampleAR: لدي ذكرى حيّة لرائحة المطبخ في بيت جدي وجدتّي.

vocabulary.definition: to cause someone to remember something from the past
vocabulary.exampleEN: That photo album brings back memories of our first trip together.
vocabulary.exampleAR: ألبوم الصور يستحضر ذكريات رحلتنا الأولى معًا.

vocabulary.definition: to think about past events
vocabulary.exampleEN: I sometimes look back on my childhood and laugh at small worries.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أحيانًا أنظر إلى طفولتي وأضحك على بعض المخاوف الصغيرة.

vocabulary.definition: to accept a difficult or unpleasant fact
vocabulary.exampleEN: It took her a long time to come to terms with the change.
vocabulary.exampleAR: استغرقت وقتًا طويلًا حتى تقبّلت التغيير.

vocabulary.definition: a friend you have known since you were a child
vocabulary.exampleEN: My childhood friend and I still meet for coffee every year.
vocabulary.exampleAR: لا يزال صديق الطفولة يلتقيني لتناول القهوة كل عام.

vocabulary.definition: a choice that has a major and lasting effect on someone's life
vocabulary.exampleEN: Moving countries was a life-changing decision for him.
vocabulary.exampleAR: الانتقال إلى بلد آخر كان قرارًا غيّر حياته.

vocabulary.definition: to become less important or remembered over time
vocabulary.exampleEN: Most small worries fade into the past as you gain experience.
vocabulary.exampleAR: معظم المخاوف الصغيرة تتلاشى مع مرور الوقت واكتساب الخبرة.

vocabulary.definition: to bring a fact or event back into your mind
vocabulary.exampleEN: I can recall the exact day we met.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أستطيع أن أستدعي اليوم الذي التقينا فيه بدقة.

vocabulary.definition: a statement admitting something that was hidden or wrong
vocabulary.exampleEN: Her confession changed how everyone saw the situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: غيّر اعترافها نظرة الجميع إلى الموقف.

vocabulary.definition: a feeling of reassurance and relaxation after a stressful event
vocabulary.exampleEN: There was a real sense of relief when the problem was fixed.
vocabulary.exampleAR: كان هناك شعور حقيقي بالارتياح عندما حُلّت المشكلة.

vocabulary.definition: a result that was not predicted or expected
vocabulary.exampleEN: The unexpected outcome of the conversation was that we became partners.
vocabulary.exampleAR: النتيجة غير المتوقعة للمحادثة أنها أدت إلى شراكتنا.

grammar.topic: narrative tenses and sequencing
grammar.concept: Use past simple for finished actions, past continuous for ongoing past actions/background, and past perfect to show an earlier past event. Combine these with sequencing words (when, while, after, before, by the time, eventually) to tell clear stories.
grammar.arabicComparison: الماضي البسيط للأحداث المكتملة، الماضي المستمر للخلفية أو حدث مستمر في الماضي، والماضي التام لحدث أقدم من حدث ماضٍ آخر. تُستخدم كلمات التسلسل لربط الأحداث بوضوح.
grammar.structure: Past simple: I went / Past continuous: I was going / Past perfect: I had gone. Sequencers: when, while, after, before, by the time, eventually, afterwards.
grammar.commonError: Choosing past simple instead of past perfect for the earlier event (wrong: 'I left when he had arrived.' Correct: 'I had left when he arrived.'), and missing clear sequencing words.
grammar.exampleEN: By the time I got to the station, the train had already left. While I was running to the platform, I realised I had forgotten my ticket.
grammar.exampleAR: بحلول الوقت الذي وصلت فيه إلى المحطة، كان القطار قد غادر بالفعل. بينما كنت أركض نحو الرصيف، أدركت أنني نسيت تذكرتي.

readingBrief: Read an original 250–350-word first-person story about a real turning point: meeting a stranger on a train who became a mentor and led to a career change. Focus on narrative tenses, sequencing markers, expressions of feeling, and how the writer organises beginning, middle and end.
writingPrompt: Write a 140–180-word email to a close friend describing a personal turning point you experienced. Purpose: tell the story (what happened), explain how you felt, and say what changed afterwards. Success criteria: use past simple, past continuous and past perfect appropriately; include at least four sequencing words (for example: when, while, after, by the time, eventually); organise your email with a clear beginning, middle and end; keep a conversational, reflective tone suitable for a friend.

title: Decisions and consequences

outcome.canDo: I can explain a decision, describe possible results, and give advice about responsibility using conditionals for real and imagined outcomes.
outcome.canDoArabic: أستطيع شرح قرار، وصف النتائج المحتملة، وتقديم نصيحة حول المسؤولية باستخدام جمل الشرط للنتائج الحقيقية والمتخيلة.
outcome.scenario: You are part of a community group deciding whether to keep a small local library open. You must explain your view, predict possible outcomes, and recommend a responsible plan the group can follow.
outcome.scenarioArabic: أنت عضو في مجموعة مجتمعية تقرر ما إذا كانت ستحافظ على مكتبة محلية صغيرة مفتوحة. عليك أن تشرح وجهة نظرك، تتنبأ بالنتائج المحتملة، وتقترح خطة مسؤولة يمكن للمجموعة اتباعها.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Briefly describe one past experience when you or a group made an important choice (what happened and why).
retrieval.purpose: Activate A2 experience language and lead into talking about consequences.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Say what you plan to do next week and one possible problem that could happen.
retrieval.purpose: Repurpose A2 plans to practise first-conditionals (real outcomes).

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Give two preferences about community services (which you like or dislike) and explain why.
retrieval.purpose: Use A2 preferences to connect opinion language with conditional advice.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Name a local service you use (e.g. library, bus, clinic). Describe one change you would make to it.
retrieval.purpose: Combine A2 services and change to prepare for proposing solutions.

network.learningNote: Teach conditionals tied to decision language: students learn to predict real outcomes (first conditional) and imagine unlikely results (second conditional) while using multi-word chunks to sound natural.
network.learningNoteArabic: علّم جمل الشرط مرتبطة بلغة اتخاذ القرار: يتعلم الطلاب التنبؤ بالنتائج الحقيقية (الشرط الأول) وتخيل النتائج غير المحتملة (الشرط الثاني) مع استخدام عبارات متعددة الكلمات لتكون اللغة طبيعية.

wordFamilies.note: Use both the verb (decide) and noun (decision) in spoken and written opinions.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: استخدم الفعل (decide) والاسم (decision) في الرأي المنطوق والمكتوب.

wordFamilies.note: Talk about who is responsible and what responsible choices look like.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: تحدث عمن هو مسؤول وكيف تبدو الخيارات المسؤولة.

wordFamilies.note: Use consider and its forms when suggesting alternatives or reviewing choices.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: استخدم consider وصيغها عند اقتراح بدائل أو إعادة النظر في الخيارات.

vocabulary.definition: to choose between two or more options after thinking
vocabulary.exampleEN: We need to make a decision about the library by Friday.
vocabulary.exampleAR: نحتاج إلى اتخاذ قرار بشأن المكتبة بحلول يوم الجمعة.

vocabulary.definition: to compare possible choices and consider their advantages and disadvantages
vocabulary.exampleEN: Before we agree, let's weigh up the options carefully.
vocabulary.exampleAR: قبل أن نتفق، دعونا نوازن الخيارات بعناية.

vocabulary.definition: to accept the results (often negative) of an action
vocabulary.exampleEN: If we close the library, the children will face the consequences of less study support.
vocabulary.exampleAR: إذا أغلقت المكتبة، سيواجه الأطفال عواقب قلة الدعم الدراسي.

vocabulary.definition: to accept duty for something and be accountable
vocabulary.exampleEN: The council must take responsibility for maintaining local services.
vocabulary.exampleAR: يجب أن تتحمل البلدية مسؤولية الحفاظ على الخدمات المحلية.

vocabulary.definition: to finally decide what you will do
vocabulary.exampleEN: I can't make up my mind about which option is best.
vocabulary.exampleAR: لا أستطيع أن أقرر أي خيار هو الأفضل.

vocabulary.definition: a result or effect of an action or decision
vocabulary.exampleEN: One consequence of losing the bus service was more people staying at home.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أحد نتائج فقدان خدمة الحافلات هو بقاء المزيد من الناس في المنزل.

vocabulary.definition: a duty or task that you are expected to manage
vocabulary.exampleEN: Shared responsibility helps local projects succeed.
vocabulary.exampleAR: المسؤولية المشتركة تساعد المشاريع المحلية على النجاح.

vocabulary.definition: a feeling of sadness or disappointment about something you did or did not do
vocabulary.exampleEN: She regrets not asking more questions before voting.
vocabulary.exampleAR: هي ندمت لعدم طرحها المزيد من الأسئلة قبل التصويت.

vocabulary.definition: the final result of a process or event
vocabulary.exampleEN: The likely outcome of the meeting is a compromise.
vocabulary.exampleAR: المحصلة المحتملة للاجتماع هي حل وسط.

vocabulary.definition: to think carefully about something before making a decision
vocabulary.exampleEN: Consider the cost and the benefits before you decide.
vocabulary.exampleAR: انظر في التكلفة والفوائد قبل أن تقرر.

vocabulary.definition: another choice or option
vocabulary.exampleEN: If we cannot raise funds, we should look for alternative solutions.
vocabulary.exampleAR: إذا لم نستطع جمع الأموال، يجب أن نبحث عن حلول بديلة.

vocabulary.definition: not planned or predicted
vocabulary.exampleEN: An unexpected problem forced them to change the plan.
vocabulary.exampleAR: مشكلة غير متوقعة أجبرتهم على تغيير الخطة.

grammar.topic: Conditionals for real and imagined outcomes
grammar.concept: Use the first conditional to talk about real possible future results (If + present, will + verb). Use the second conditional to imagine unlikely or hypothetical situations and their imagined results (If + past simple, would + verb).
grammar.arabicComparison: في العربية نستخدم 'إذا' مع الأزمنة المناسبة؛ الفرق المهم هو أن الشرط الأول يتكلم عن وضع حقيقي ممكن في المستقبل، أما الشرط الثاني فيتخيل موقفًا غير حقيقي أو غير محتمل.
grammar.structure: First conditional: If + present simple, will + base verb. Second conditional: If + past simple, would + base verb.
grammar.commonError: Students often use 'will' in the if-clause (incorrect: If it will rain...) or use past simple when they should use present for first conditional.
grammar.exampleEN: First: If the council agrees, we will keep the library open. Second: If I were in charge, I would organize community events at the library.
grammar.exampleAR: الأول: إذا وافقت البلدية، فسنحافظ على المكتبة مفتوحة. الثاني: لو كنت المسؤول، لأقمت فعاليات مجتمعية في المكتبة.

readingBrief: Read an original 250–350-word article telling the story of a small town deciding whether to close its local library. The article should present three different viewpoints (a parent, a retired teacher, and a young student), describe possible short- and long-term outcomes, and include at least four conditional sentences (both first and second conditional). The text will help learners identify how people weigh options, accept responsibility, and predict consequences.
writingPrompt: Write a 140–180-word letter to the local council explaining your view on keeping the library open. Audience: local council members. Purpose: state your decision, predict two possible outcomes (use at least one first conditional and one second conditional), and recommend one responsible action the council should take. Success criteria: organise your letter with a short introduction, two clear body paragraphs (one for outcomes, one for recommendation), and a concluding sentence; use a polite formal tone throughout.

title: People, boundaries, and trust

outcome.canDo: I can explain a disagreement, describe boundaries I need, and suggest a practical solution while using relative clauses and polite disagreement language.
outcome.canDoArabic: أستطيع شرح خلاف، ووصف الحدود التي أحتاجها، واقتراح حل عملي مع استخدام الجمل التابعة (relative clauses) وعبارات الاعتراض بأدب.
outcome.scenario: You are part of a local volunteer group where a disagreement about sharing resources has damaged trust. You must describe what happened, say what boundaries you want, and propose a fair plan to rebuild trust.
outcome.scenarioArabic: أنت عضو في مجموعة تطوعية محلية حدث خلاف بشأن مشاركة الموارد وأثر ذلك على الثقة. عليك وصف ما حدث، وذكر الحدود التي تريدها، واقتراح خطة عادلة لإعادة بناء الثقة.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Think of an experience when you disagreed with a friend or colleague. What happened? Who was involved? (Use 2–3 short sentences.)
retrieval.purpose: Retrieve an A2-level experience to expand into a connected B1 narrative.

retrieval.language: Arabic
retrieval.prompt: اذكر تجربة حصل فيها نقاش أو خلاف مع صديق أو زميل. ماذا حدث؟ من كان متورطًا؟ (جملتان أو ثلاث).
retrieval.purpose: استدعاء تجربة A2 لتوسيعها لسرد متصل على مستوى B1.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: What would you prefer if a team member keeps using your things without asking? Say one preferred solution.
retrieval.purpose: Turn a simple preference into a plan that includes setting boundaries and proposing steps.

retrieval.language: Arabic
retrieval.prompt: ما تفضّل لو استمر عضو الفريق في استخدام أغراضك دون أن يسأل؟ اذكر حلًا واحدًا تفضّله.
retrieval.purpose: تحويل تفضيل بسيط إلى خطة تتضمن وضع حدود واقتراح خطوات.

network.learningNote: At B1 we connect simple preferences and experiences to reasons and consequences. Teach phrases that show respect while disagreeing (e.g. 'I see your point, but...') and practise relative clauses to add detail about people and situations.
network.learningNoteArabic: في مستوى B1 نربط التفضيلات والتجارب البسيطة بالأسباب والنتائج. درّس عبارات تُظهر الاحترام أثناء الاعتراض (مثل «أفهم وجهة نظرك، لكن...») ودرّب على الجمل التابعة لإضافة تفاصيل عن الأشخاص والمواقف.

wordFamilies.note: Use 'trust' as verb and noun; 'trusted' describes people or things that others rely on.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: استخدم 'trust' كفعل واسم؛ 'trusted' تصف أشخاصًا أو أشياء يمكن الاعتماد عليها.

wordFamilies.note: Support can be practical or emotional; collocations (show support, give support) are common.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: قد يكون الدعم عمليًا أو عاطفيًا؛ التضامن مع collocations مثل «show support» و«give support» شائع.

wordFamilies.note: At B1, contrast 'agree' and 'disagree' politely and use 'agreement' in proposals.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: في مستوى B1 قارن بين 'agree' و 'disagree' بأدب واستخدم 'agreement' عند الاقتراحات.

vocabulary.definition: a limit that defines acceptable behaviour between people
vocabulary.exampleEN: We need clear boundaries about shared equipment.
vocabulary.exampleAR: نحتاج إلى حدود واضحة بشأن المعدات المشتركة.

vocabulary.definition: to explain limits you need in a relationship or group
vocabulary.exampleEN: She set boundaries with new volunteers to avoid confusion.
vocabulary.exampleAR: وضعت حدودًا مع المتطوعين الجدد لتجنب الالتباس.

vocabulary.definition: to behave in a way that ignores someone else's limit
vocabulary.exampleEN: When he borrowed tools without asking, he crossed a boundary.
vocabulary.exampleAR: عندما استعار الأدوات دون أن يسأل، تجاوز حدًا.

vocabulary.definition: respect that two or more people give to each other
vocabulary.exampleEN: Mutual respect helped the team solve the problem calmly.
vocabulary.exampleAR: ساعد الاحترام المتبادل الفريق على حل المشكلة بهدوء.

vocabulary.definition: to allow someone time or distance to think or calm down
vocabulary.exampleEN: After the argument, I decided to give him some space.
vocabulary.exampleAR: بعد الخلاف قررت أن أمنحه بعض المساحة.

vocabulary.definition: to develop confidence between people over time
vocabulary.exampleEN: Small promises kept can build trust in a group.
vocabulary.exampleAR: الوعود الصغيرة التي تُوفى تبني الثقة في المجموعة.

vocabulary.definition: to say politely that you are worried about something
vocabulary.exampleEN: She voiced a concern about how decisions were made.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أعربت عن قلقها بشأن كيفية اتخاذ القرارات.

vocabulary.definition: to help someone emotionally or practically; help
vocabulary.exampleEN: The group offered support to the new members.
vocabulary.exampleAR: قدمت المجموعة الدعم للأعضاء الجدد.

vocabulary.definition: to speak to someone directly about a problem, often strongly
vocabulary.exampleEN: I didn't want to confront him, so I wrote a note instead.
vocabulary.exampleAR: لم أرغب في مواجهته، فكتبت ملاحظة بدلًا من ذلك.

vocabulary.definition: an agreement where each side gives up something
vocabulary.exampleEN: They reached a compromise that suited both teams.
vocabulary.exampleAR: توصلوا إلى حل توفيقي يناسب كلتا الفرق.

vocabulary.definition: the ability to understand and share another person's feelings
vocabulary.exampleEN: Empathy helped her listen without judging.
vocabulary.exampleAR: ساعدها التعاطف على الاستماع دون إصدار أحكام.

vocabulary.definition: a friend you can rely on and confide in
vocabulary.exampleEN: I spoke to a trusted friend before deciding what to say.
vocabulary.exampleAR: تحدثت إلى صديق موثوق قبل أن أقرر ماذا أقول.

grammar.topic: relative clauses and polite disagreement
grammar.concept: Use relative clauses to add essential or extra information about people or things, and use polite disagreement phrases to show respect while expressing a different view.
grammar.arabicComparison: الجمل التابعة تضيف معلومات عن الأشخاص أو الأشياء، وعبارات الاعتراض بأدب تسمح بقول رأي مخالف دون إساءة.
grammar.structure: Relative clause (defining): noun + who/that/which + verb (e.g. 'the volunteer who organised the rota'); Relative clause (non-defining): noun + , which/who + verb, + , (e.g. 'Sami, who is reliable, offered to help'); Polite disagreement: phrases such as 'I see your point, but...', 'I understand that, however...', 'I’m not sure I agree because...'.
grammar.commonError: Mixing relative clause punctuation: omitting commas for non-defining clauses; starting a polite disagreement too directly (e.g. 'You're wrong') instead of softening language.
grammar.exampleEN: I appreciate your idea, which is thoughtful, but I’m not sure it will work in our schedule. The coordinator who arranged the meeting was not available.
grammar.exampleAR: أقدّر فكرتك، وهي فكرة مدروسة، لكن لست متأكدًا أنها ستنجح في جدولنا. المنسق الذي رتّب الاجتماع لم يكن متاحًا.

readingBrief: Read an original 250–350-word story about a community garden group that disagreed over how to share tools. The piece follows three members: the organiser who set rules, a volunteer who felt ignored, and a neighbour who crossed a boundary. It shows how they voice concerns, set clear boundaries, and slowly build trust through small promises. Focus on identifying: who did what, which boundaries mattered, and examples of polite disagreement and relative clauses used to explain situations.
writingPrompt: Write a 140–180-word email to the group coordinator explaining a recent disagreement, stating one boundary you need, and proposing two practical steps to rebuild trust. Audience: group coordinator. Purpose: report the problem and suggest a fair plan. Success criteria: organise your email into a short introduction, one paragraph describing the issue with at least one relative clause, and one paragraph with two clear steps; keep a respectful, polite tone (use phrases such as 'I understand your point, but...' or 'I appreciate that, however...').

title: Changing a habit

outcome.canDo: I can tell a connected story about trying to change a habit, describe setbacks and support I used, and give a short plan for staying motivated using used to, would and the present perfect continuous.
outcome.canDoArabic: أستطيع أن أسرد قصة مترابطة حول محاولتي تغيير عادة، وأصف النكسات والدعم الذي استخدمته، وأقدّم خطة قصيرة للحفاظ على الدافع باستخدام used to و would والزمن المضارع التام المستمر.
outcome.scenario: A colleague asks for your advice after several failed attempts to stop checking their phone at work. You tell a short connected story about your own experience, explain what went wrong, suggest practical solutions and a two-week plan to try.
outcome.scenarioArabic: زميل في العمل يطلب نصيحتك بعد عدة محاولات فاشلة لوقف تفقد هاتفه أثناء العمل. تروي قصة قصيرة مترابطة عن تجربتك، تشرح ما حدث خطأ، وتقترح حلولاً عملية وخطة لمدة أسبوعين للتجربة.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Tell a 2-minute story about a time you tried to change a daily habit (experience). Say what you planned and whether the plan worked (plans, change).
retrieval.purpose: Activate A2 experience and plan language and push for a connected past-to-present narrative.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Explain which new routine you prefer now and why (preferences, opinions). Give one example of a problem you had and your opinion about the best solution.
retrieval.purpose: Use simple preference and opinion language but expand with reasons and examples.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Describe a service or support you used (a gym, coach, app) to help change your habit. Say how it helped and one downside (services, opinions).
retrieval.purpose: Move A2 service descriptions toward evaluating usefulness and drawbacks.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Talk about a recent change you have been making (change). Say how long you have been trying and one small success so far.
retrieval.purpose: Encourage present perfect continuous and progress language for ongoing change.

network.learningNote: Use used to and would for past repeated actions or states (past habits). Use the present perfect continuous (have/has been + -ing) to talk about actions that started in the past and continue now. For advice and plans, use practical collocations such as set a goal and stick to a plan.
network.learningNoteArabic: استخدم used to و would للأعمال المتكرّرة أو الحالات في الماضي (عادات قديمة). استخدم المضارع التام المستمر (have/has been + -ing) للأفعال التي بدأت في الماضي وتستمر الآن. عند إعطاء نصيحة واستراتيجية، استخدم تراكيب مفيدة مثل set a goal و stick to a plan.

wordFamilies.note: Verb and related noun/adjective forms useful for talking about reasons to continue.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: فعل وصيغ اسمية ووصفيّة متعلقة، مفيدة للحديث عن أسباب الاستمرار.

wordFamilies.note: Core verb and adjective forms used for habits and routines.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: الفعل الأساسي وصيغته الوصفية المستخدمة للحديث عن العادات والروتين.

wordFamilies.note: Useful for talking about returning to an old habit after a period of change.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: مفيد للحديث عن العودة إلى عادة قديمة بعد فترة من التغير.

vocabulary.definition: Stop doing a repeated behaviour that you have done for a long time.
vocabulary.exampleEN: She wanted to break a habit of checking social media during meetings.
vocabulary.exampleAR: كانت تريد الإقلاع عن عادة تفقد وسائل التواصل أثناء الاجتماعات.

vocabulary.definition: Begin again, often without intending to, an old behaviour or routine.
vocabulary.exampleEN: After two weeks away, he slipped back into old eating habits.
vocabulary.exampleAR: بعد أسبوعين بعيدًا، عاد تدريجيًا إلى عادات الأكل القديمة.

vocabulary.definition: Decide on a clear and achievable target to work towards.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Set a goal to reduce screen time by 30 minutes each day.
vocabulary.exampleAR: حدّد هدفًا لتقليل وقت الشاشة بمقدار 30 دقيقة يوميًا.

vocabulary.definition: Continue following a planned set of actions without giving up.
vocabulary.exampleEN: If you stick to a plan, small progress soon becomes a habit.
vocabulary.exampleAR: إذا تمسكت بالخطة، يصبح التقدم الصغير عادة قريبًا.

vocabulary.definition: Return to the correct course of action after an interruption or setback.
vocabulary.exampleEN: After a weekend of poor sleep, she worked hard to get back on track.
vocabulary.exampleAR: بعد عطلة نهاية أسبوع نامت فيها قليلًا، عملت جاهدة للعودة إلى المسار.

vocabulary.definition: A regular behaviour or practice, often done without thinking.
vocabulary.exampleEN: A morning coffee is a habit for many people.
vocabulary.exampleAR: القهوة الصباحية عادة لدى كثير من الناس.

vocabulary.definition: A problem or delay that makes progress more difficult.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Missing a day of exercise felt like a setback, but she continued the next day.
vocabulary.exampleAR: شعرت بأن تفويت يوم من التمرين كان نكسة، لكنها واصلت في اليوم التالي.

vocabulary.definition: Something that causes a behaviour or emotion to start.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Stress is a common trigger for unhealthy eating.
vocabulary.exampleAR: التوتر محفز شائع للأكل غير الصحي.

vocabulary.definition: Reasons or energy that make someone want to do something.
vocabulary.exampleEN: She found motivation in small wins each day.
vocabulary.exampleAR: وجدت الدافع في الانتصارات الصغيرة كل يوم.

vocabulary.definition: A regular sequence of actions or activities.
vocabulary.exampleEN: A fixed evening routine helped him relax and sleep better.
vocabulary.exampleAR: ساعده روتين مسائي ثابت على الاسترخاء والنوم بشكل أفضل.

vocabulary.definition: A return to a previous bad habit after a period of improvement.
vocabulary.exampleEN: A small relapse doesn't mean failure; it means you need a new strategy.
vocabulary.exampleAR: الانتكاس الصغير لا يعني الفشل؛ بل يعني أن عليك استراتيجية جديدة.

vocabulary.definition: Continued effort to do or achieve something despite difficulties.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Perseverance helped him keep trying even after setbacks.
vocabulary.exampleAR: ساعدته المثابرة على الاستمرار حتى بعد النكسات.

grammar.topic: used to, would, and present perfect continuous
grammar.arabicName: used to و would والمضارع التام المستمر
grammar.concept: used to and would describe past habits or repeated actions. used to can describe past states as well. would is often used for past repeated actions in stories. The present perfect continuous (have/has been + -ing) describes actions that started in the past and continue now or were happening recently.
grammar.arabicComparison: تُستخدم used to و would لوصف عادات متكررة في الماضي؛ used to يمكن أن تصف حالات ماضية أيضًا. would مناسب للسرد. يُستخدم المضارع التام المستمر (have/has been + -ing) لأفعال بدأت في الماضي وتستمر حتى الآن أو حدثت مؤخرًا.
grammar.structure: used to + base verb; would + base verb (for past repeated actions); have/has been + verb-ing (for ongoing past-to-present actions).
grammar.commonError: Using used to for actions that continue now (wrong) or using would for past states (would usually cannot replace used to for states). Confusing simple past with present perfect continuous when an action continues now.
grammar.exampleEN: Used to: I used to go for a run every morning. Would: When I was a student, I would study late into the night. Present perfect continuous: I have been trying to run three times a week for two months.
grammar.exampleAR: Used to: اعتدت أن أركض كل صباح. Would: عندما كنت طالبًا، كنت أذاكر حتى وقت متأخر من الليل. المضارع التام المستمر: أحاول الركض ثلاث مرات في الأسبوع منذ شهرين.

readingBrief: Read a 250–350 word original interview with a woman who changed her afternoon snack habit. The interview should include: a short background (what she used to do), the trigger that made her try to change, two specific setbacks, the small strategies she used (support, goals, routines), and a reflection on progress after three months. The piece must show cause-and-effect (why something failed or worked) and use used to, would and at least two examples of present perfect continuous.
writingPrompt: Write a 140–180 word informal email to a classmate describing one habit you are trying to change. Purpose: explain what you used to do, describe at least one setback and one small success, and give a two-week plan to improve. Success criteria: organise your email with a short opening (what the habit was), a middle paragraph (what you tried and setbacks), and a closing paragraph (your two-week plan and a friendly tone). Try to use used to, would and the present perfect continuous at least once each if possible.

title: Seeing it differently

outcome.canDo: I can give a balanced, qualified opinion about a local issue, use hedging language, and link contrasting ideas clearly.
outcome.canDoArabic: أستطيع أن أعبر عن رأي متوازن ومؤهّل بشأن قضية محلية، وأستخدم تعابير التحفّظ، وأربط الأفكار المتعارضة بوضوح.
outcome.scenario: The town council plans to redevelop the central park. You need to write an email to the community board giving a considered view that recognises other opinions, presents at least one piece of evidence or personal experience, and suggests a practical compromise.
outcome.scenarioArabic: تفكر البلدية في إعادة تطوير الحديقة المركزية. عليك كتابة بريد إلكتروني إلى مجلس المجتمع تبدي فيه رأياً مدروساً يعترف بآراء الآخرين، ويقدّم دليلاً أو تجربة شخصية واحدة على الأقل، ويقترح حلاً عملياً متوسطاً.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Describe one experience you had in the past year with a local service (e.g., library, bus, park). Say what you liked and what you would change.
retrieval.purpose: Activate A2 experience language to prepare details you can use as evidence in a B1 opinion.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Talk about a plan you had that changed. What happened and why did you change your plans?
retrieval.purpose: Reuse A2 plan vocabulary to practise explaining reasons and showing contrast.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Tell the class about a preference you have for quiet versus busy public places and why.
retrieval.purpose: Recycle A2 preference language so learners can qualify opinions with reasons.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Describe a time you used a local service (e.g., a café, a bus route). Were you satisfied? Give one fact that supports your view.
retrieval.purpose: Encourage retrieval of factual evidence from A2-level descriptions to use in B1 argument.

network.learningNote: Hedging softens certainty (it seems, might, could); contrast linkers (on the other hand, however, nonetheless) show a controlled discussion. Use hedges when you can't prove something and contrast linkers to compare viewpoints.
network.learningNoteArabic: التعبيرات التحفّظية تُخفّف من التأكيد (it seems, might, could)؛ روابط التباين (on the other hand, however, nonetheless) تُظهر مناقشة متزنة. استخدم التحفّظ حين لا يمكنك إثبات أمرٍ ما، وروابط التباين لمقارنة وجهات النظر.

wordFamilies.note: Use to explain reasons or evidence that support a claim.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: يُستخدم لشرح الأسباب أو الأدلة التي تدعم ادعاءً.

wordFamilies.note: To add limits or conditions to a statement (e.g., 'I agree, but...').
wordFamilies.noteArabic: إضافة حدود أو شروط لبيان (مثل: 'أوافق، لكن...').

wordFamilies.note: Shows hesitation; useful when giving a careful opinion.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: يُظهر التردد؛ مفيد عند إعطاء رأي حذر.

vocabulary.definition: to fully agree with someone
vocabulary.exampleEN: I don't see eye to eye with the council on the design, but I respect their efforts.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أنا لا أوافق المجلس تمامًا بشأن التصميم، لكني أحترم جهوده.

vocabulary.definition: to consider something when making a decision
vocabulary.exampleEN: We should take into account the villagers' daily routines before changing bus times.
vocabulary.exampleAR: يجب أن نأخذ بعين الاعتبار روتين السكان اليومي قبل تغيير مواعيد الحافلات.

vocabulary.definition: used to introduce a contrasting point
vocabulary.exampleEN: The plan would reduce costs. On the other hand, it might harm the local market.
vocabulary.exampleAR: الخطة ستقلل التكاليف. من ناحية أخرى، قد تضر بالسوق المحلي.

vocabulary.definition: to make people less certain about something
vocabulary.exampleEN: Recent reports cast doubt on the claimed environmental benefits.
vocabulary.exampleAR: تقارير حديثة أثارت الشكوك حول الفوائد البيئية المزعومة.

vocabulary.definition: a polite way to give a personal opinion
vocabulary.exampleEN: It seems to me that adding more trees would be a sensible compromise.
vocabulary.exampleAR: يبدو لي أن إضافة المزيد من الأشجار سيكون حلاً وسطًا معقولاً.

vocabulary.definition: information that supports or proves something
vocabulary.exampleEN: The council provided evidence about safety, but residents asked for more studies.
vocabulary.exampleAR: قدّم المجلس دلائل حول السلامة، لكن السكان طالبوا بمزيد من الدراسات.

vocabulary.definition: a statement that something is true, often needing proof
vocabulary.exampleEN: Her claim that the shops will close quickly needs supporting evidence.
vocabulary.exampleAR: ادعاؤها بأن المحلات ستغلق سريعًا يحتاج إلى أدلة داعمة.

vocabulary.definition: to show or explain why something is reasonable or necessary
vocabulary.exampleEN: The council must justify the budget if residents are to accept the cuts.
vocabulary.exampleAR: على المجلس أن يبرر الميزانية إذا كان السكان سيقبلون التخفيضات.

vocabulary.definition: unwilling or hesitant to do something
vocabulary.exampleEN: Some shop owners are reluctant to support the plan because of uncertainty.
vocabulary.exampleAR: بعض أصحاب المحلات مترددون في دعم الخطة بسبب عدم اليقين.

vocabulary.definition: a small but important difference in meaning or tone
vocabulary.exampleEN: It's important to notice the nuance between 'possible' and 'likely' in reports.
vocabulary.exampleAR: من المهم ملاحظة الفارق الدقيق بين 'ممكن' و'مرجح' في التقارير.

vocabulary.definition: to limit or modify a statement so it is less absolute
vocabulary.exampleEN: I agree with the idea, but I'd like to qualify my support with a condition.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أوافق على الفكرة، لكني أود قيد دعمي بشرط.

vocabulary.definition: in spite of what has just been said; nevertheless
vocabulary.exampleEN: There are risks; nonetheless, the project could bring long-term benefits.
vocabulary.exampleAR: هناك مخاطر؛ مع ذلك، قد يجلب المشروع فوائد طويلة الأجل.

grammar.topic: Hedging and contrast linkers
grammar.concept: Use hedging language (it seems, might, could, I tend to) to make opinions less absolute. Use contrast linkers (on the other hand, however, nonetheless) to compare or balance opposing ideas.
grammar.arabicComparison: استخدم عبارات التحفّظ (it seems, might, could, I tend to) لجعل الآراء أقل مطلقية. استخدم روابط التباين (on the other hand, however, nonetheless) لمقارنة أو موازنة الأفكار المتعارضة.
grammar.structure: Hedging: It seems to me that + clause / I might be wrong, but + clause / modal (could, might) + verb. Contrast linkers: Statement A. On the other hand, statement B. / Statement; however, contrasting statement.
grammar.commonError: Learners often use strong certainties (always, definitely) instead of hedges, or place contrast linkers incorrectly inside clauses rather than between balanced ideas.
grammar.exampleEN: Hedge: 'I might be wrong, but the park seems underused.' Contrast: 'The plan would increase visitors. However, it could raise noise levels.'
grammar.exampleAR: مثال للتحفّظ: 'قد أكون مخطئًا، لكن الحديقة تبدو غير مستخدمة بشكل كافٍ.' مثال للتباين: 'ستزيد الخطة عدد الزائرين. مع ذلك، قد تزيد مستويات الضجيج.'

readingBrief: Read an original 250–350-word interview with three local people (a resident, a shop owner, and a council planner) about a proposed park redevelopment. The interview presents differing opinions and short pieces of evidence (e.g., survey results, personal routines, sales figures). Identify hedging language, at least two contrast linkers, and write a one-paragraph summary (40–60 words) stating the overall balance of views.
writingPrompt: Write an email (140–180 words) to the community board giving your qualified opinion about the park redevelopment. Audience: community board members. Purpose: present your view, acknowledge other perspectives, give at least one piece of evidence or a short personal experience, and suggest a practical compromise. Success criteria: organise your email into three short paragraphs (intro with your position, one paragraph with two supporting points/evidence using hedging, final paragraph with a clear suggestion), and keep a respectful, persuasive tone throughout.

title: A message that matters

outcome.canDo: I can write and respond to emails that make a clear request, choosing a formal or informal tone appropriately and organising my message so the recipient knows what action to take.
outcome.canDoArabic: أستطيع كتابة والرد على رسائل إلكترونية تحتوي طلباً واضحاً، واختيار الأسلوب الرسمي أو غير الرسمي بشكل مناسب وتنظيم الرسالة حتى يعرف المتلقّي الإجراء المطلوب.
outcome.scenario: You receive an email about a change that affects you (a workshop time, a service arrangement, or a group project). You must write a reply explaining your situation, request a reasonable adjustment, and suggest a practical solution. Your message needs the right degree of politeness and clear organisation so the recipient can act.
outcome.scenarioArabic: تتلقّى رسالة إلكترونية عن تغيير يؤثّر عليك (موعد ورشة عمل، ترتيب خدمة، أو مشروع جماعي). يجب أن تكتب رداً تشرح فيه وضعك، وتطلب تعديلاً مناسباً وتقترح حلاً عملياً. يجب أن تكون رسالتك بالمستوى المناسب من اللباقة ومنظمة بوضوح حتى يتمكّن المستلم من اتخاذ إجراء.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Think of a recent experience (A2: experience). In one sentence, describe what happened and one problem you faced.
retrieval.purpose: Recall simple past verbs and experience vocabulary to use as background in your B1 email.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Describe a plan you have for next week (A2: plans). Say when it starts and one thing that might change it.
retrieval.purpose: Prepare time and change vocabulary you can explain when asking for a time adjustment.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Say one preference you have for meeting times or ways of working (A2: preferences).
retrieval.purpose: Activate language for polite choices (I prefer…, I’d rather…) useful for making requests.

retrieval.language: Arabic
retrieval.prompt: صف خدمة استخدمتها مؤخراً (A2: services) — ما أعجبك وما لم يعجبك؟
retrieval.purpose: استدعاء مفردات مناسبة لخدمة وملاحظات عملية تستخدمها عند تقديم شكوى أو طلب تعديل.

network.learningNote: Choose verbs and modals to match the level of politeness: use 'Could you / Would you mind / I would appreciate it if' in formal emails; use 'Can you / Could you do me a quick favour' with colleagues or friends. Organise short paragraphs: reason, request, and suggested action.
network.learningNoteArabic: اختر الأفعال والأدوات التعبيرية حسب مستوى اللباقة: استخدم 'Could you / Would you mind / I would appreciate it if' في رسائل رسمية؛ واستخدم 'Can you / Could you do me a quick favour' مع الزملاء أو الأصدقاء. قم بتنظيم الفقرات: السبب، الطلب، والإجراء المقترح.

wordFamilies.note: Use as noun (a request) or verb (to request). In formal writing, 'request' and 'would appreciate' are common.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: تُستخدم كاسم (a request) أو فعل (to request). في الكتابة الرسمية شائع 'request' و 'would appreciate'.

wordFamilies.note: Useful for asking for or offering more information: 'Could you clarify…' or 'For clarification, see…'.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: مفيدة لطلب أو تقديم مزيد من المعلومات: 'Could you clarify…' أو 'For clarification, see…'.

wordFamilies.note: Common in emails to signal files: 'Please find attached' (formal) or 'I've attached' (neutral).
wordFamilies.noteArabic: شائعة في البريد الإلكتروني للإشارة إلى الملفات: 'Please find attached' (رسمي) أو 'I've attached' (محايد).

vocabulary.definition: to point out a problem or worry to someone so it can be addressed
vocabulary.exampleEN: I need to raise a concern about the room booking for Friday.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أحتاج إلى إثارة قلق بشأن حجز الغرفة ليوم الجمعة.

vocabulary.definition: to check the status of something after an earlier action or message
vocabulary.exampleEN: I'll follow up on your application next week and let you know the outcome.
vocabulary.exampleAR: سأتابع بشأن طلبك الأسبوع القادم وأعلمك بالنتيجة.

vocabulary.definition: an informal, short request asking someone to do something small
vocabulary.exampleEN: Could I ask a quick favour? Could you check the link for me?
vocabulary.exampleAR: هل لي بطلب صغير؟ هل يمكنك التحقق من الرابط لي؟

vocabulary.arabic: في وقت مناسب / في الوقت المناسب
vocabulary.definition: within an appropriate or expected time; without unnecessary delay
vocabulary.exampleEN: Please respond in a timely manner so we can confirm the booking.
vocabulary.exampleAR: يرجى الرد في الوقت المناسب حتى نتمكن من تأكيد الحجز.

vocabulary.definition: to give formal approval for someone to do something
vocabulary.exampleEN: The manager granted permission for us to change the meeting date.
vocabulary.exampleAR: منح المدير الإذن لنا لتغيير موعد الاجتماع.

vocabulary.definition: the attitude or manner expressed in speaking or writing
vocabulary.exampleEN: Adjust your tone: make it formal for the client and friendlier for classmates.
vocabulary.exampleAR: غيّر نبرتك: اجعلها رسمية مع العميل وألطف مع زملاء الدراسة.

vocabulary.definition: to make something clear or easier to understand
vocabulary.exampleEN: Could you clarify the timeslot you mean by 'afternoon'?
vocabulary.exampleAR: هل يمكنك توضيح الفاصل الزمني الذي تقصده بـ 'بعد الظهر'؟

vocabulary.definition: a belief about what should happen or be achieved
vocabulary.exampleEN: We need to set clear expectations for who will lead the task.
vocabulary.exampleAR: نحتاج إلى وضع توقعات واضحة حول من سيقود المهمة.

vocabulary.definition: needing immediate attention
vocabulary.exampleEN: Label the message 'urgent' only if it needs immediate action.
vocabulary.exampleAR: عَلِّم الرسالة بـ 'عاجل' فقط إذا كانت تحتاج إلى إجراء فوري.

vocabulary.definition: a file sent together with an email
vocabulary.exampleEN: Please see the attachment for the revised timetable.
vocabulary.exampleAR: يرجى الاطلاع على المرفق للاطلاع على الجدول المعدّل.

vocabulary.definition: showing good manners in speech or behaviour
vocabulary.exampleEN: Be polite and specific when you ask for help.
vocabulary.exampleAR: كن لبقاً ومحدداً عندما تطلب المساعدة.

vocabulary.definition: a statement asking for something to be given or done
vocabulary.exampleEN: I would like to request an extension until next Tuesday.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أود أن أطلب تمديداً حتى يوم الثلاثاء القادم.

grammar.topic: Formal and informal requests
grammar.concept: Different language forms (modals, polite phrases, and tone) change how a request is received. Use more indirect and formal structures in professional emails and simpler direct forms with friends or colleagues.
grammar.arabicComparison: تغيّر أدوات اللغة (الأدوات الشرطية، عبارات اللباقة، والنبرة) كيفية استقبال الطلب. استخدم تراكيب أكثر لباقة وغير مباشرة في الرسائل المهنية وتراكيب أبسط مع الأصدقاء.
grammar.structure: Formal: 'I would appreciate it if you could + base verb' or 'Could you please + base verb?' Informal: 'Can you + base verb?' or 'Could you do me a quick favour and + base verb?' Use 'Would you mind + -ing' to be polite and indirect.
grammar.commonError: Mixing registers (e.g. starting formally then using very direct imperatives) or using 'please' only at the end which can sound abrupt. Avoid multiple negatives or vague requests without a clear action.
grammar.exampleEN: Formal: 'I would appreciate it if you could send the report by Monday.' Informal: 'Can you send me the report on Monday? Thanks!'
grammar.exampleAR: رسمي: 'أقدّر لو تكرمت بإرسال التقرير بحلول يوم الاثنين.' غير رسمي: 'هل يمكنك إرسال التقرير يوم الاثنين؟ شكراً!'

readingBrief: A single original email of 250–350 words written by a course coordinator to participants. The email explains a sudden change to a workshop schedule, gives reasons (venue double-booking and staff illness), offers two alternative dates, asks participants to state their preference, and requests a quick confirmation by a clear deadline. The article demonstrates shifting tone (polite/formal at the start, slightly more casual when suggesting the quick favour), uses formal request forms ('I would appreciate it if') and informal follow-up language ('If this is a problem, let me know'), and includes an attached updated timetable. Learners should notice request language, phrases that soften tone, and the organisation into reason, options, request, and closing.
writingPrompt: Write an email (140–180 words) to your course coordinator asking for a change to a scheduled meeting or deadline. Audience: course coordinator (formal). Purpose: explain your situation, request a specific adjustment, and suggest a practical solution or alternative time. Success criteria: organise your email in clear short paragraphs (opening reason, specific request, suggested solution, polite closing) and use an appropriately formal tone with at least one polite request form (e.g. 'I would appreciate it if...').

title: A better neighbourhood

outcome.canDo: I can use modal verbs (obligation, advice, possibility) to explain local priorities, suggest solutions, and argue for change in my neighbourhood.
outcome.canDoArabic: أستطيع استخدام الأفعال الناقصة (الوجوب، النصيحة، الاحتمال) لشرح الأولويات المحلية، واقتراح حلول، والدفاع عن تغييرات في حيي.
outcome.scenario: You are part of a residents' group writing to the local council and speaking at a community meeting about improvements. You must explain problems, suggest practical steps, and judge which actions are most important.
outcome.scenarioArabic: أنت عضو في مجموعة سكان تكتب إلى مجلس البلدية وتتحدث في اجتماع مجتمعي عن التحسينات. يجب عليك شرح المشكلات، اقتراح خطوات عملية، وتقييم أي الإجراءات أكثر أهمية.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Describe one experience you had using a local service (e.g. bus, library, recycling). Say what happened and whether it was helpful.
retrieval.purpose: Recall A2 experience vocabulary and set a real example to build a B1 argument about local services.

retrieval.language: العربية
retrieval.prompt: اخبر عن خطة بسيطة لديك لتحسين جزء من الحي (مثل تنظيف أو زراعة). ماذا ستفعل؟
retrieval.purpose: استرجاع لغة التخطيط من مستوى A2 قبل تحويلها إلى اقتراحات أكثر قوة باستخدام أفعال ناقصة.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Say which local facility you prefer (e.g. park, market) and why. Mention one thing you would change.
retrieval.purpose: Use A2 preferences and tie them to a B1 discussion about priorities and changes.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Describe a recent change in the area (new shop, roadworks). Say whether people liked it or not.
retrieval.purpose: Recall language for 'change' and prepare material for a connected narrative that leads to recommendations.

network.learningNote: At B1, modal verbs let you qualify suggestions and responsibilities clearly. Use must/have to for obligation, should/ought to for advice, and might/could/may for possibility. Combine them with multi-word chunks (e.g. 'take action on') to make practical proposals.
network.learningNoteArabic: في مستوى B1، تساعد الأفعال الناقصة على تحديد الاقتراحات والمسؤوليات بوضوح. استخدم must/ have to للوجوب، should/ ought to للنصيحة، وmight/ could/ may للاحتمال. اربطها بتعابير متعددة الكلمات مثل 'take action on' لاقتراح حلول عملية.

wordFamilies.note: Improve (verb) → improvement (noun): common when talking about local projects.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: improve فعل → improvement اسم: شائع عند الحديث عن مشاريع محلية.

wordFamilies.note: Repair often collocates with buildings, roads and services (carry out repairs).
wordFamilies.noteArabic: repair كثيراً ما يتجاور مع المباني والطرق والخدمات (carry out repairs).

wordFamilies.note: Safety is a noun used when prioritising neighbourhood concerns.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: safety اسم يستخدم عند تحديد أولويات القلق في الحي.

vocabulary.definition: Buses, trams, trains and other transport that is available to the public.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Better public transport links would make it easier for residents to get to work.
vocabulary.exampleAR: روابط نقل عام أفضل ستجعل من السهل على السكان الوصول إلى أماكن عملهم.

vocabulary.definition: A park or area with grass and trees for people to enjoy.
vocabulary.exampleEN: The new green space in the centre is well used by families.
vocabulary.exampleAR: المساحة الخضراء الجديدة في المركز يستخدمها العائلات بشكل جيد.

vocabulary.definition: Homes offered at lower cost so people on modest incomes can afford them.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Residents asked the council to build more affordable housing near schools.
vocabulary.exampleAR: طلب السكان من المجلس بناء المزيد من الإسكان الميسور التكلفة قرب المدارس.

vocabulary.definition: Facilities and support provided in the area, such as libraries, bins, and street-cleaning.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Good local services make day-to-day life much easier for older residents.
vocabulary.exampleAR: الخدمات المحلية الجيدة تسهل الحياة اليومية كثيراً على السكان المسنين.

vocabulary.definition: To do something practical to solve a problem.
vocabulary.exampleEN: If we take action now, we may be able to stop the flooding next winter.
vocabulary.exampleAR: إذا اتخذنا إجراءً الآن، فقد نتمكن من منع الفيضانات في الشتاء القادم.

vocabulary.definition: To try to persuade an organisation or person to act.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Residents put pressure on the council to fix the broken crossings.
vocabulary.exampleAR: ضغط السكان على المجلس لإصلاح المعابر المكسورة.

vocabulary.definition: To make something better.
vocabulary.exampleEN: We should improve street lighting on the high street.
vocabulary.exampleAR: ينبغي أن نحسّن إنارة الشوارع في الشارع الرئيسي.

vocabulary.definition: A change that makes something better.
vocabulary.exampleEN: The recent improvement to the playground has attracted more families.
vocabulary.exampleAR: التحسّن الأخير في ملعب الأطفال جذب المزيد من العائلات.

vocabulary.definition: To fix something that is broken or damaged.
vocabulary.exampleEN: The council must repair the potholes on Hayfield Road.
vocabulary.exampleAR: يجب على المجلس إصلاح الحفر في طريق هايفيلد.

vocabulary.definition: The condition of being protected from danger or risk.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Safety for cyclists should be a top priority when redesigning the roads.
vocabulary.exampleAR: يجب أن تكون سلامة ركاب الدراجات أولوية قصوى عند إعادة تصميم الطرق.

vocabulary.definition: A person who rents a home or flat from a landlord.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Tenants in the block said they must have regular repairs to heating systems.
vocabulary.exampleAR: قال المستأجرون في المبنى إن عليهم الحصول على إصلاحات منتظمة لأنظمة التدفئة.

vocabulary.definition: Local government authority responsible for public services and planning.
vocabulary.exampleEN: The council announced a consultation on local road safety next month.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أعلن المجلس عن استشارة بشأن سلامة الطرق المحلية الشهر المقبل.

grammar.topic: Modals for obligation, advice, and possibility
grammar.concept: Use must/have to for obligation; should/ought to for advice; might/could/may for possibility. Choose form to show strength of obligation or uncertainty.
grammar.arabicComparison: استخدم must/ have to للوجوب القوي، should/ ought to للنصيحة الخفيفة، وmight/ could/ may للقول بالاحتمال أو عدم اليقين.
grammar.structure: modal + base verb (must/should/might + verb). 'Have to' uses auxiliary (have/has + to + verb) for present obligations.
grammar.commonError: Learners often use 'must' and 'should' interchangeably. 'Must' shows strong obligation; 'should' is a suggestion. Also mixing 'might' with present simple for future possibility is incorrect.
grammar.exampleEN: Obligation: The council must repair the pavement. Advice: You should tell the councillor about the broken light. Possibility: We might get funding for a new playground.
grammar.exampleAR: الوجوب: يجب على المجلس إصلاح الرصيف. النصيحة: يجب أن تخبر العضو عن الإضاءة المكسورة. الاحتمال: قد نحصل على تمويل لملعب جديد.

readingBrief: Read a 250–350-word interview with a local campaigner who organised a successful community project. The interview should describe the problem (poor lighting and litter), the steps the group took (letter to council, petition, weekend clean-up), obstacles (limited funds, mixed opinions), and three lessons for other residents. Expect concrete examples, modal verbs for advice and possibility, and a clear conclusion about priorities.
writingPrompt: Write a 140–180-word formal email to your local councillor describing one important problem in your neighbourhood and suggesting two practical actions the council should take. Audience: local councillor. Purpose: persuade the council to act. Success criteria: organise the email into at least three short paragraphs (problem - suggestions - closing), use a polite formal tone, and include at least three modal verbs that show obligation, advice, and possibility (e.g. must / should / might).

title: Working with different people

outcome.canDo: I can describe roles and solve a simple team problem, report what others said in a meeting, and suggest a fair course of action.
outcome.canDoArabic: أستطيع وصف الأدوار وحل مشكلة بسيطة في الفريق، نقل كلام الآخرين في اجتماع، واقتراح حل عادل.
outcome.scenario: Your team missed a deadline because members had different workstyles and unclear responsibilities. In a short meeting you must explain what happened, report colleagues' views, and propose steps to avoid the same problem.
outcome.scenarioArabic: فريقك أخفق في تسليم مهمة لأن أساليب العمل مختلفة والمسؤوليات غير واضحة. في اجتماع قصير عليك شرح ما حدث، نقل آراء الزملاء، واقتراح خطوات لتجنّب المشكلة نفسها.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Think of a time you worked with others (experience). Write two or three short notes: what you did, one problem you had, and one suggestion you made.
retrieval.purpose: Repurpose A2 'experiences' into a B1 task by preparing concise notes you can report in a meeting.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Describe your plan (plans) for dividing a small project between three people. Use simple bullet points.
retrieval.purpose: Use A2 'plans' but organize them so you can later report decisions and responsibilities to the team.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Say which working conditions you prefer (preferences): quiet workspace, clear deadlines, or frequent check-ins. Give one reason.
retrieval.purpose: Repurpose A2 'preferences' into a supported opinion you can report and compare with others in a meeting.

retrieval.language: Arabic
retrieval.prompt: ذكّر موقفاً طلبت فيه خدمة من زميل (services). اكتب جملة واحدة عن ما طلبته وكيف استجابت.
retrieval.purpose: تحويل A2 'الخدمات' إلى ملبية احتياج اجتماعي في الاجتماع: تتيح نقل ما طلبته وكيف كان ردّ الزملاء.

network.learningNote: Focus on multi-word verbs and set phrases used in meetings (e.g. 'chair a meeting', 'follow up'). For reported speech, practise changing present-tense comments to suitable reporting verbs and backshift when necessary.
network.learningNoteArabic: ركّز على الأفعال المركبة والعبارات المستخدمة في الاجتماعات (مثل «يدير الاجتماع»، «يتابع»). عند استخدام الكلام المنقول، غيّر الزمن عند الحاجة واستخدم أفعال تقرير مناسبة.

wordFamilies.note: Use 'agree' and 'agreement' to show consensus; 'disagree' to report objections.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: استخدم 'agree' و 'agreement' لإظهار التوافق، و 'disagree' لنقل الاعتراضات.

wordFamilies.note: Useful for describing how team members share information and for reporting methods (e.g. 'She suggested communicating by email').
wordFamilies.noteArabic: مفيد لوصف كيفية تبادل المعلومات والإشارة إلى وسائل التواصل (مثلاً «اقترحت أن نتواصل عبر البريد»).

wordFamilies.note: Use 'lead' and 'leader' to describe roles; 'leadership' for responsibilities and qualities.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: استخدم 'lead' و 'leader' لوصف الأدوار؛ و 'leadership' للحديث عن المسؤوليات والصفات.

vocabulary.definition: do something one after another so each person has an opportunity
vocabulary.exampleEN: In the meeting we decided to take turns presenting sections of the report.
vocabulary.exampleAR: في الاجتماع قررنا أن نتناوب على عرض أجزاء التقرير.

vocabulary.definition: find an agreement acceptable to all or most team members
vocabulary.exampleEN: After a long discussion, the team reached a consensus on the deadline.
vocabulary.exampleAR: بعد نقاش طويل، توصل الفريق إلى إجماع بشأن الموعد النهائي.

vocabulary.definition: bring attention to a problem or topic that needs discussion
vocabulary.exampleEN: She raised an issue about overlapping responsibilities.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أثارت مسألة حول تداخل المسؤوليات.

vocabulary.definition: act as the person who leads and organises a meeting
vocabulary.exampleEN: He volunteered to chair the meeting and keep the discussion focused.
vocabulary.exampleAR: تطوع ليلترأس الاجتماع ويجعل النقاش مركزاً.

vocabulary.definition: check progress after an action or remind someone about an agreed task
vocabulary.exampleEN: I'll follow up with an email after the meeting.
vocabulary.exampleAR: سأتابع برسالة إلكترونية بعد الاجتماع.

vocabulary.definition: make clear what is expected from each person or about outcomes
vocabulary.exampleEN: We need to set expectations for who will do each task.
vocabulary.exampleAR: نحتاج إلى تحديد التوقعات بشأن من سينفذ كل مهمة.

vocabulary.definition: manage disagreements between people constructively
vocabulary.exampleEN: The manager suggested training to help staff handle conflict better.
vocabulary.exampleAR: اقترح المدير تدريباً لمساعدة الموظفين على التعامل مع الصراع بشكل أفضل.

vocabulary.definition: the way a person prefers to work (e.g. independently or collaboratively)
vocabulary.exampleEN: Different working styles caused delays in the project.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أدت أساليب العمل المختلفة إلى تأخير المشروع.

vocabulary.definition: discuss until you reach an agreement, often about responsibilities or deadlines
vocabulary.exampleEN: They negotiated who would take the difficult tasks.
vocabulary.exampleAR: تفاوضوا بشأن من سيتولى المهام الصعبة.

vocabulary.definition: to identify shared opinions or interests so people can agree and work together
vocabulary.exampleEN: He said they needed to find common ground before the next meeting.
vocabulary.exampleAR: قال إنهم بحاجة إلى إيجاد أرضية مشتركة قبل الاجتماع القادم.

vocabulary.definition: a person who helps a group discuss and decide, without making decisions for them
vocabulary.exampleEN: The facilitator kept the meeting on track and invited quieter members to speak.
vocabulary.exampleAR: حافظ الميسر على سير الاجتماع ودعا الأعضاء الأكثر هدوءاً للتحدث.

vocabulary.definition: a person who belongs to a team with shared responsibilities
vocabulary.exampleEN: Each team member was given a clear task and deadline.
vocabulary.exampleAR: تم تكليف كل عضو في الفريق بمهمة واضحة وموعد نهائي.

grammar.topic: Reported speech for meetings
grammar.concept: How to report what people said in meetings: choose a reporting verb, shift tenses and pronouns when necessary, and keep the reported content concise.
grammar.arabicComparison: عند نقل كلام آخرين في اجتماع، نستخدم أفعال تقرير مناسبة ونغير الأزمنة والضمائر إذا لزم الأمر، ونبقي الكلام المختصر واضحاً.
grammar.structure: Reporting verb + that + [subject] + [past tense (if backshift)] / For commands: reporting verb + (object) + to + base verb / For questions: reporting verb + wh-word + clause (change word order, use 'asked' or 'wanted to know').
grammar.commonError: Not backshifting tenses (e.g. saying 'She says that we will finish' instead of 'She said that we would finish') and keeping questions in direct order when reporting.
grammar.exampleEN: Direct: "I need more time," John said. Reported: John said (that) he needed more time. Direct: "Can you finish this by Friday?" the manager asked. Reported: The manager asked if we could finish it by Friday.
grammar.exampleAR: مباشر: «أحتاج مزيداً من الوقت» قال جون. منقول: قال جون إنه احتاج مزيداً من الوقت. مباشر: «هل تستطيعون إنجاز هذا بحلول الجمعة؟» سأل المدير. منقول: سأل المدير إن كنا نستطيع إنجاز ذلك بحلول الجمعة.

readingBrief: Read an original 250–350-word interview with a project team leader about how they resolved a missed deadline caused by different working styles and unclear roles. The piece should include at least three short direct quotes from team members and the leader, descriptions of practical steps taken (reassigning tasks, setting expectations, a follow-up plan), and examples of reported speech summarising team members' opinions. Focus: understanding how people explain causes, report others' comments, and describe concrete solutions.
writingPrompt: Write a 140–180-word email to your team after a short meeting. Audience: your project team. Purpose: summarise what happened, report two colleagues' suggestions using reported speech, and propose a clear follow-up plan. Success criteria: organise the email with a short opening, a paragraph reporting others' views (use reported speech for at least two statements), and a final paragraph with precise action points and polite, collaborative tone.

title: Explaining a problem clearly

outcome.canDo: I can explain a service problem in a clear, chronological way, use passive forms to describe what happened, and suggest practical solutions.
outcome.canDoArabic: أستطيع شرح مشكلة في خدمة بوضوح وبترتيب زمني، واستخدام المبني للمجهول لوصف ما حدث، واقتراح حلول عملية.
outcome.scenario: You are writing to a company about a repeated service failure. You must give a timeline, describe what was done (including actions by staff), and request a clear remedy.
outcome.scenarioArabic: أنت تكتب لشركة بخصوص فشل متكرر في خدمة. يجب أن تقدّم جدولًا زمنيًا، وتصف ما تمّ عمله (بما في ذلك إجراءات الموظفين)، وتطلب حلًا واضحًا.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Think of a recent experience (A2: experiences) where a service did not meet your expectations. Briefly note: what happened, when, and who you contacted.
retrieval.purpose: Activate simple past narrative to use as material for a more detailed, linked B1 explanation.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Describe any plans you had around the time of the problem (A2: plans). Did the issue force a change of those plans? Make two sentences about the change.
retrieval.purpose: Turn A2 planning language into cause-and-effect in a short sequence for the B1 task.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Say which service option you usually prefer (A2: preferences) and why. Then add one sentence about how the problem affected that preference.
retrieval.purpose: Link simple preferences to a qualified opinion in a B1 explanation.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: List any services or people you contacted (A2: services, people). For each, write one sentence describing what they did or did not do.
retrieval.purpose: Prepare facts to form a clear timeline and passive descriptions in the B1 writing.

network.learningNote: At B1 we link simple past A2 narratives into a clear, ordered account. Use chronological markers (first, then, after that) and passives to focus on actions taken rather than people — useful in complaints.
network.learningNoteArabic: في مستوى B1 نربط السرد البسيط للماضي (A2) إلى سرد منظم زمنيًا. استخدم أدوات الترتيب الزمني (أولاً، ثم، بعد ذلك) والمبني للمجهول للتركيز على الإجراءات بدلاً من الأشخاص — وهذا مفيد في الشكاوى.

wordFamilies.note: complain (verb) and complaint (noun) are both common in service language; complainant = person making the complaint.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: complain فعل و complaint اسم. complainant = صاحب الشكوى.

wordFamilies.note: Use resolved/resolution when talking about the final outcome; resolved (adjective) describes an issue that has been fixed.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: استخدم resolved/ resolution عند الحديث عن النتيجة النهائية؛ resolved تصف مشكلة تم حلّها.

wordFamilies.note: Notification (noun) is the record of being informed; be notified of + event is a common passive structure.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: notification = إشعار. be notified of + حدث يُستخدم كثيرًا في المبني للمجهول.

vocabulary.definition: to officially report a problem to an organisation
vocabulary.exampleEN: I had to file a complaint after the second service outage.
vocabulary.exampleAR: اضطررت لتقديم شكوى بعد انقطاع الخدمة للمرة الثانية.

vocabulary.definition: to pass a problem to a higher level of authority for faster action
vocabulary.exampleEN: If the issue is not resolved, the case will be escalated to a manager.
vocabulary.exampleAR: إذا لم تُحل المشكلة، سيتم تصعيد الحالة إلى مدير.

vocabulary.definition: a temporary stop or interruption in a service
vocabulary.exampleEN: A service outage affected our internet last night.
vocabulary.exampleAR: تسبّب انقطاع الخدمة في تأثر الإنترنت لدينا الليلة الماضية.

vocabulary.definition: a short-term solution that is not permanent
vocabulary.exampleEN: The technician applied a temporary fix while waiting for parts.
vocabulary.exampleAR: قام الفني بتطبيق حل مؤقت أثناء انتظار القطع.

vocabulary.definition: to correct a problem or repair something
vocabulary.exampleEN: We expect the fault to be put right within 48 hours.
vocabulary.exampleAR: نتوقع أن يتم إصلاح العطل خلال ٤٨ ساعة.

vocabulary.definition: to be informed about an event or decision
vocabulary.exampleEN: You will be notified of any follow-up appointments by email.
vocabulary.exampleAR: سيتم إخطرك بأي مواعيد متابعة عبر البريد الإلكتروني.

vocabulary.definition: technical help given by someone who is not physically present
vocabulary.exampleEN: Remote support was offered to diagnose the software problem.
vocabulary.exampleAR: تم تقديم الدعم عن بُعد لتشخيص مشكلة البرنامج.

vocabulary.definition: a skilled worker who repairs or maintains equipment
vocabulary.exampleEN: A technician visited yesterday to inspect the equipment.
vocabulary.exampleAR: زار فني أمس لفحص الجهاز.

vocabulary.definition: Repayment of money paid for a service or product; to return money to someone.
vocabulary.exampleEN: After the service was cancelled, a full refund was issued to all affected customers.
vocabulary.exampleAR: بعد إلغاء الخدمة، تم إصدار رد المبلغ بالكامل لجميع العملاء المتضررين.

vocabulary.definition: the action of solving a problem or the final decision
vocabulary.exampleEN: A satisfactory resolution was reached after the second inspection.
vocabulary.exampleAR: تم التوصّل إلى حل مُرضٍ بعد الفحص الثاني.

vocabulary.definition: to confirm that something (e.g., a message or problem) has been received
vocabulary.exampleEN: Please acknowledge receipt of this email and the fault report.
vocabulary.exampleAR: يرجى تأكيد استلام هذا البريد الإلكتروني وتقرير العطل.

vocabulary.definition: remaining to be resolved or completed
vocabulary.exampleEN: There are two outstanding issues that still need attention.
vocabulary.exampleAR: هناك مسألتان قيد المتابعة لا تزالان بحاجة للاهتمام.

grammar.topic: Passives in practical communication
grammar.concept: Use passive forms to focus on actions or outcomes (what was done) rather than on who did them. Common in complaints and service communication.
grammar.arabicComparison: يُستخدم المبني للمجهول للتركيز على الفعل أو النتيجة بدلاً من صاحب الفعل، وهو مناسب عند تقديم الشكاوى أو وصف الإجراءات.
grammar.structure: Subject + be (present/past/modal) + past participle (e.g., 'The fault was reported', 'You will be notified')
grammar.commonError: Learners often omit the auxiliary 'be' or mix tense (e.g., 'The problem reported' instead of 'The problem was reported'). Also confusing when to include the agent ('by...').
grammar.exampleEN: The issue was reported on 12 July, and a technician was sent the same day.
grammar.exampleAR: تم الإبلاغ عن المشكلة في 12 يوليو، وتم إرسال فني في نفس اليوم.

readingBrief: Read an original 250–350-word email from a customer to a utility company. The email describes a recurring service outage over three weeks, gives a clear timeline with dates and previous contacts, summarises actions taken by both the customer and the company (using passive and active forms), explains the impact on the customer's plans, and requests a permanent solution or compensation. The tone is formal but firm.
writingPrompt: Write a 140–180-word formal email to the customer service team of a provider. Audience: customer service manager. Purpose: explain a recurring problem clearly, give a timeline of events (at least three dated points), describe what has been done (use at least two passive constructions), and request a specific solution (repair, replacement, refund or compensation). Success criteria: organise the email with a brief opening, a chronological timeline paragraph, an impact/request paragraph, and a polite closing; maintain a professional, firm tone.

title: Work that fits

outcome.canDo: I can describe my skills and preferences, explain which jobs suit me, and use gerunds and infinitives correctly when talking about work decisions.
outcome.canDoArabic: أستطيع وصف مهاراتي وتفضيلاتي، وشرح أي وظيفة تناسبني، واستخدام الأسماء المصدرية والمصدر مع to بشكل صحيح عند الحديث عن قرارات العمل.
outcome.scenario: You are preparing a short portfolio and email for a careers adviser. You must explain your experience, show which jobs would suit you and ask for two pieces of practical advice. Use gerunds and infinitives correctly when explaining past actions and future plans.
outcome.scenarioArabic: أنت تُعِد حقيبة عمل ورسالة إلكترونية لمستشار مهني. عليك شرح خبراتك، وبيان الوظائف المناسبة لك، وطلب نصيحتين عمليتين. استخدم الأسماء المصدرية والمصدر مع to بشكل صحيح عند شرح الأعمال السابقة والخطط المستقبلية.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: List two past experiences (jobs, volunteering or courses) and one thing you learned from each.
retrieval.purpose: Activate A2 vocabulary for experiences as a basis for a connected B1 description of skills.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Write two short plans for the next six months about finding work (e.g. update CV; contact agencies).
retrieval.purpose: Repurpose simple planning language into concrete steps for a B1 action plan.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Say three job preferences (hours, environment, pay) and explain one preference with a reason.
retrieval.purpose: Turn basic preference statements into justified opinions useful for choosing a job.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Name two services you used when looking for work (e.g. job centre, online CV builder) and say whether they helped.
retrieval.purpose: Retrieve service vocabulary and evaluate effectiveness; prepares learners to describe support in a B1 task.

network.theme: skills, strengths and choosing a suitable job
network.learningNote: Focus on useful chunks (e.g. 'apply for a job', 'make a good impression') and practise verbs that take gerunds or infinitives in job contexts (e.g. enjoy working / decide to apply).
network.learningNoteArabic: ركّز على العبارات المفيدة (مثل «التقدم لوظيفة»، «ترك انطباع جيد») وتدرّب على الأفعال التي تتبعها أسماء مصدرية أو مصدر مع to في سياق العمل (مثال: enjoy working / decide to apply).

wordFamilies.note: Commonly used with 'for' (apply for a job) and appears in noun and agent forms.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: تُستخدم عادةً مع 'for' (apply for a job) وتظهر بصيغ اسمية وصيغة الفاعل.

wordFamilies.note: Useful for talking about judging skills or candidates in interviews and tests.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: مفيدة للحديث عن تقييم المهارات أو المتقدمين في المقابلات والاختبارات.

wordFamilies.note: Shows flexibility; 'adaptable' is a strong adjective to include in applications.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: تظهر المرونة؛ «قابل للتكيف» صفة قوية يُستحسن ذكرها في الطلبات.

vocabulary.definition: Skills you can use in different jobs or situations.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Her transferable skills include communication and problem-solving.
vocabulary.exampleAR: تشمل مهاراتها القابلة للنقل التواصل وحل المشكلات.

vocabulary.definition: Work with fewer hours than a full-time job.
vocabulary.exampleEN: He prefers part-time work while he studies for his degree.
vocabulary.exampleAR: يفضل العمل بدوام جزئى أثناء دراسته للحصول على الدرجة.

vocabulary.definition: A form or document used to apply for a job.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Send your job application before the closing date.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أرسل طلب التوظيف قبل تاريخ الإغلاق.

vocabulary.definition: A series of jobs and roles that form someone's professional life.
vocabulary.exampleEN: She is considering teaching as a long-term career path.
vocabulary.exampleAR: تفكر في التدريس كمسار مهني طويل الأجل.

vocabulary.definition: To behave or present yourself so others think positively of you.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Dress smartly to make a good impression at the interview.
vocabulary.exampleAR: ارتدِ ملابس أنيقة لترك انطباع جيد في المقابلة.

vocabulary.definition: An email sent after a meeting or interview to thank or remind.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Send a polite follow-up email the day after your interview.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أرسل رسالة متابعة مهذبة بعد يوم من المقابلة.

vocabulary.definition: Appropriate or right for a particular person or purpose.
vocabulary.exampleEN: This part-time role is suitable for students.
vocabulary.exampleAR: هذه الوظيفة بدوام جزئى مناسبة للطلاب.

vocabulary.definition: To evaluate or judge the quality or ability of someone or something.
vocabulary.exampleEN: The panel will assess each candidate's skills and experience.
vocabulary.exampleAR: سيقوم الفريق بتقييم مهارات وخبرات كل مرشح.

vocabulary.definition: Able to change to suit new conditions or situations.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Employers value workers who are adaptable and willing to learn.
vocabulary.exampleAR: يقدر صاحب العمل الموظفين القابلين للتكيف والراغبين في التعلم.

vocabulary.definition: A position or set of responsibilities in a job or group.
vocabulary.exampleEN: In this role you'll manage a small team and report to the director.
vocabulary.exampleAR: في هذه الوظيفة ستدير فريقًا صغيرًا وتقدم تقاريرك للمدير.

vocabulary.definition: The total pay and benefits offered by an employer.
vocabulary.exampleEN: We discussed the salary package including pension and holiday pay.
vocabulary.exampleAR: ناقشنا حزمة الراتب بما في ذلك المعاش وإجازات العمل.

vocabulary.definition: A promise or duty to do something; the time someone agrees to give.
vocabulary.exampleEN: A full-time job requires a serious time commitment.
vocabulary.exampleAR: الوظيفة بدوام كامل تتطلب التزامًا زمنيًا جادًا.

grammar.topic: Gerunds and infinitives after verbs
grammar.concept: Some verbs are followed by a gerund (verb+ing), some by an infinitive (to + verb), and a few can take both with little or big change in meaning. Use then to talk about likes, decisions and plans in job contexts.
grammar.arabicComparison: بعض الأفعال يتبعها الاسم المصدر (-ing)، وبعضها يتبعه المصدر مع to، وبعضها يقبل الاثنين مع تغيير بسيط أو كبير في المعنى.
grammar.structure: Common patterns: enjoy + verb-ing (enjoy working); decide + to + verb (decide to apply); stop + verb-ing (stop working) vs stop + to + verb (stop to make a call).
grammar.commonError: Using -ing after verbs that need to + infinitive (e.g. I want going → correct: I want to go). Also mixing meanings (I stopped to smoke ≠ I stopped smoking).
grammar.exampleEN: I enjoy working with people, so I decided to apply for the customer-service role.
grammar.exampleAR: أستمتع بالعمل مع الناس، لذلك قررت التقدم لوظيفة خدمة العملاء.

readingBrief: Read an original 250–350 word interview between a career adviser and a job-seeker exploring how to find work that fits their strengths. The text includes specific examples of transferable skills, job options (full-time, part-time), and a short sequence of decisions the job-seeker took (e.g. volunteering, updating a CV, contacting employers). The article demonstrates gerunds and infinitives in context (for example: 'I enjoy volunteering' / 'I decided to apply') and shows how to structure a short, persuasive personal narrative about career choices.
writingPrompt: Write a 140–180 word email to a careers adviser. Purpose: summarise your most relevant skills and experience, explain what type of job would suit you and ask for two practical suggestions (e.g. where to apply, how to prepare). Audience: a professional careers adviser at a local job centre. Success criteria: organise the email into three short paragraphs (intro + strengths, suitable job + reason, clear request), keep a polite, professional tone, and include one sentence with a gerund and one with an infinitive.

title: Making a proposal
