outcome.canDo: I can make a short proposal, linking purpose and expected result, and explain benefits and risks to persuade others.
outcome.canDoArabic: أستطيع أن أقدّم اقتراحًا قصيرًا، أربط الغرض بالنتيجة المتوقعة، وأشرح الفوائد والمخاطر لإقناع الآخرين.
outcome.scenario: You are a member of a community group. The town council has a small grant for local projects. You must propose a weekend project that helps residents, explain why it is needed, show benefits and risks, and recommend next steps.
outcome.scenarioArabic: أنت عضو في مجموعة مجتمعية. لدى مجلس المدينة منحة صغيرة للمشروعات المحلية. عليك أن تقترح مشروعًا عطليًا يساعد السكان، وتشرح لماذا هو مطلوب، وتعرض الفوائد والمخاطر، وتقترح خطوات تالية.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Tell a partner about a service you used recently (e.g., library, café). Say what you liked and what you would change.
retrieval.purpose: Repurpose A2: use a simple experience to generate ideas for improvements before making a proposal.

retrieval.language: Arabic
retrieval.prompt: احكِ لشريك عن خطة بسيطة قمت بها في الأسبوع الماضي (مثل تنظيف الحديقة أو ترتيب مكتبة). ماذا نجح؟ ماذا لم ينجح؟
retrieval.purpose: استرجاع خبرة (A2) لتحديد نقاط قوة وضعف تُستخدم لاحقًا في اقتراح جودة أو تغيير.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Name one change you prefer in your neighbourhood (A2 preference). Now explain one reason this change would help others and one possible problem it could cause.
retrieval.purpose: Move from preferences to qualified opinion: link a desired change with benefit and risk.

retrieval.language: Arabic
retrieval.prompt: اخبر الآخرين برأيك في خدمة محلية (مثل المواصلات أو الترييض) وتحدث عن فائدة واحدة ومخاطرة واحدة متعلقة بتحسين هذه الخدمة.
retrieval.purpose: استخدام آراء (A2) لصياغة وصف موجز للفوائد والمخاطر قبل كتابة اقتراح.

network.learningNote: Focus on linking purpose (why) with likely result (what will happen). Use connectors like 'in order to' or 'so that' for purpose and 'therefore' or 'as a result' for result. Be explicit about who benefits and what might go wrong.
network.learningNoteArabic: ركّز على ربط الغرض (لماذا) بالنتيجة المتوقعة (ماذا سيحدث). استخدم أدوات الربط مثل «in order to» أو «so that» للغرض و«therefore» أو «as a result» للنتيجة. كن واضحًا بشأن المستفيدين وما قد يسوء.

wordFamilies.note: Use 'benefit' to name an advantage; 'beneficial' to describe something positive.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: استخدم 'benefit' لذكر ميزة؛ و'beneficial' لوصف شيء إيجابي.

wordFamilies.note: 'Mitigate' is often used with risks: you mitigate risks (reduce them).
wordFamilies.noteArabic: يُستخدم 'mitigate' مع المخاطر: تعني تقليلها.

wordFamilies.note: 'Implementation' is the noun for the process of putting a plan into action.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: 'Implementation' اسم للعملية التي تقوم فيها بتطبيق الخطة.

vocabulary.definition: To suggest a plan or idea formally to others.
vocabulary.exampleEN: At the meeting, I will make a proposal to start weekend classes.
vocabulary.exampleAR: سأقدم اقتراحًا لبدء دروس نهاية الأسبوع في الاجتماع.

vocabulary.definition: To give reasons and evidence to support an idea.
vocabulary.exampleEN: She presented a strong case for a community garden.
vocabulary.exampleAR: قدمت حُجّة قوية من أجل حديقة مجتمعية.

vocabulary.definition: To carefully consider the possible problems or dangers.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Before agreeing, we need to weigh the risks of the event.
vocabulary.exampleAR: قبل الموافقة، نحتاج لتقييم مخاطر الحدث.

vocabulary.definition: To put a decided plan into action.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Volunteers will carry out the plan next month.
vocabulary.exampleAR: سيقوم المتطوعون بتنفيذ الخطة الشهر القادم.

vocabulary.definition: To come to a mutual decision after discussion.
vocabulary.exampleEN: After the discussion, we reached an agreement on dates.
vocabulary.exampleAR: بعد المناقشة، توصلنا إلى اتفاق بشأن المواعيد.

vocabulary.definition: to include something when considering or planning
vocabulary.exampleEN: When we make the proposal, we must factor in ongoing maintenance costs so the project stays within budget.
vocabulary.exampleAR: عند تقديم الاقتراح، يجب أن نأخذ بعين الاعتبار تكاليف الصيانة المستمرة لكي يبقى المشروع ضمن الميزانية.

vocabulary.definition: An advantage; to help or be helpful to someone or something.
vocabulary.exampleEN: One benefit of the project is more green space.
vocabulary.exampleAR: إحدى فوائد المشروع مساحة خضراء أكثر.

vocabulary.definition: A possibility of harm or loss; to expose to danger.
vocabulary.exampleEN: There is a risk of flooding in low areas.
vocabulary.exampleAR: هناك خطر فيضانات في المناطق المنخفضة.

vocabulary.definition: To make a problem or its effects less severe.
vocabulary.exampleEN: We can mitigate noise by scheduling work for daytime.
vocabulary.exampleAR: يمكننا تقليل الضوضاء بجدولة العمل في النهار.

vocabulary.definition: To put a plan or system into operation.
vocabulary.exampleEN: The council will implement the new waste scheme next year.
vocabulary.exampleAR: سيطبق المجلس نظام النفايات الجديد العام القادم.

vocabulary.definition: A person or group that has an interest in a project or decision.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Local businesses are important stakeholders in this plan.
vocabulary.exampleAR: الشركات المحلية هي أصحاب مصلحة مهمة في هذه الخطة.

vocabulary.definition: the likely or expected outcome of a plan or action
vocabulary.exampleEN: The projected result of extending opening hours is increased customer satisfaction and higher sales.
vocabulary.exampleAR: النتيجة المتوقعة لتمديد ساعات العمل هي زيادة رضا العملاء وارتفاع المبيعات.

grammar.topic: Linking a proposal with purpose and result
grammar.concept: Use purpose clauses (in order to, so that, so as to) to explain why you propose something, and result connectors (therefore, as a result, consequently, which will) to show the expected outcome.
grammar.arabicComparison: استخدم عبارات الغرض (in order to، so that) لتوضيح سبب الاقتراح، وعبارات النتيجة (therefore، as a result) لتبيان النتيجة المتوقعة.
grammar.structure: Purpose: 'We propose X in order to/so that + subject + verb.' Result: 'This will/so + clause; therefore/as a result + clause.' Example connectors: in order to, so that, therefore, as a result, consequently, which will.
grammar.commonError: Using 'so' alone for purpose (e.g., 'we did this so improve' instead of 'so that we could improve') or mixing subject positions after 'so that'. Also, confuse 'because' (reason) with 'so that' (purpose).
grammar.exampleEN: We propose a Saturday language café in order to help recent arrivals practise English, so that they can feel more confident when using services. As a result, attendance at local classes is likely to increase.
grammar.exampleAR: نقترح إقامة مقهى لغوي يوم السبت من أجل مساعدة القادمين الجدد على ممارسة الإنجليزية، حتى يشعروا بثقة أكبر عند استخدام الخدمات. ونتيجة لذلك، من المرجح أن يزداد حضور الدروس المحلية.

readingBrief: Read an original 250–350-word email from a community group leader to the town council proposing a weekend community garden project. The email explains the purpose, outlines three main benefits (social, environmental, practical), discusses two risks and how to mitigate them, names key stakeholders, and requests a meeting to agree next steps. Tone: professional but friendly.
writingPrompt: Write a 140–180-word proposal email to your community centre manager proposing a one-day-a-week weekend class or activity (e.g., language café, gardening club). Audience: centre manager. Purpose: outline the idea, link the purpose to expected results, explain at least two benefits and one risk with a way to mitigate it, and ask for permission or a meeting. Success criterion: organise the email clearly with labelled paragraphs (purpose, benefits, risks, request) and use a polite, slightly formal tone.

title: Helping beyond yourself

outcome.canDo: I can describe volunteering projects, explain their impact, and give a reasoned opinion about whether a community action is worth supporting using defining and non-defining relative clauses.
outcome.canDoArabic: أستطيع وصف مشاريع التطوع، وشرح تأثيرها، وإبداء رأي مبرّر حول ما إذا كانت مبادرة مجتمعية تستحق الدعم باستخدام الجمل الوصفية المعرفة وغير المعرفة.
outcome.scenario: You read an interview with the coordinator of a grassroots project that supports elderly people. You need to write an email to the local council (formal) proposing a related volunteer initiative and to explain why it will help, using defining and non-defining relative clauses to add detail.
outcome.scenarioArabic: تقرأ مقابلة مع منسق مشروع شعبي يدعم المسنّين. تحتاج إلى كتابة بريد إلكتروني إلى المجلس المحلي (رسمي) تقترح فيه مبادرة تطوعية ذات صلة وتشرح لماذا ستساعد، مستخدمًا الجمل الوصفية المعرفة وغير المعرفة لإضافة التفاصيل.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Remember one short experience where you helped someone (A2: I helped at a food bank). Now, in two linked sentences, describe what you did and what you felt afterwards. Aim to connect these A2 ideas into a B1 mini-story.
retrieval.purpose: Activate A2 experience language and transform it into a connected personal narrative (B1).

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Think of a simple plan you have (A2: I will help next month). Expand it into a clear plan with steps and a reason: who will do what and why. Use three sentences to show the plan and its benefit.
retrieval.purpose: Repurpose A2 plans into a short, sequenced plan with purpose (B1).

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: List one preference about how you like to help (A2: I prefer hands-on work). Then explain, in two sentences, a situation where that preference matters and what you would change if needed.
retrieval.purpose: Turn an A2 preference into a qualified opinion that considers alternatives.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Name a local service you know (A2: community centre). Describe, in two sentences, how a volunteer project could complement that service and solve a practical problem.
retrieval.purpose: Use A2 service vocabulary to suggest a practical civic solution (B1).

network.anchor: How volunteers can support local needs beyond their usual circle
priorLevelLinks: Experiences: talking about past helping activities
Plans: simple future plans to help
Preferences: saying how you prefer to help
Services: naming local services (e.g., food bank, community centre)
Opinions: short statements about what is good or bad
network.learningNote: Focus on joining clauses with defining (no commas) and non-defining (with commas) relative clauses to add precise or extra information; practise both in formal and informal registers.
network.learningNoteArabic: ركّز على ربط الجمل باستخدام الجمل الوصفية المعرفة (بدون فواصل) وغير المعرفة (مع فواصل) لإضافة معلومات دقيقة أو إضافية؛ مارس الاثنين بصيغة رسمية وغير رسمية.

wordFamilies.note: Use the verb for actions (I volunteer) and the noun for people (a volunteer). 'Voluntary' describes unpaid work.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: استخدم الفعل للأفعال (I volunteer) والاسم للأشخاص (a volunteer). 'Voluntary' تصف عملًا غير مدفوع الأجر.

wordFamilies.note: Impact can be a noun or a verb; use collocations like 'long-term impact' or 'make an impact'.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: يمكن أن يكون 'impact' اسمًا أو فعلًا؛ استخدم تراكيب مثل 'long-term impact' أو 'make an impact'.

wordFamilies.note: ‘Sustainable’ describes projects that last over time. Talk about environmental or social sustainability.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: 'Sustainable' تصف مشاريع تستمر مع الوقت. تكلم عن الاستدامة البيئية أو الاجتماعية.

vocabulary.definition: to have a noticeable, positive effect on a situation or person
vocabulary.exampleEN: A small weekly visit can really make a difference to someone who lives alone.
vocabulary.exampleAR: زيارة أسبوعية صغيرة يمكن أن تُحدث فرقًا فعلاً لشخص يعيش بمفرده.

vocabulary.definition: to return support or help to a community or group that has helped you
vocabulary.exampleEN: After finishing university, she wanted to give back to the neighbourhood that supported her.
vocabulary.exampleAR: بعد التخرج أرادت أن تُعيد الجميل للحي الذي دعمها.

vocabulary.definition: to start participating in an activity or project
vocabulary.exampleEN: More people are getting involved in local clean-up days each year.
vocabulary.exampleAR: المزيد من الناس ينخرطون في أيام تنظيف الحي كل عام.

vocabulary.definition: a community-led initiative that starts at local level rather than from large organisations
vocabulary.exampleEN: The grassroots movement, which began with a few neighbours, now supports dozens of families.
vocabulary.exampleAR: الحركة القاعدية، التي بدأت بعدد قليل من الجيران، تدعم الآن عشرات العائلات.

vocabulary.definition: a local building where people meet for activities and services
vocabulary.exampleEN: The community centre, which is open every weekday, offers free classes for older adults.
vocabulary.exampleAR: المركز المجتمعي، الذي يفتح أيام الأسبوع، يقدم دروسًا مجانية لكبار السن.

vocabulary.definition: an organisation that raises funds or provides services for people in need
vocabulary.exampleEN: We worked with a charitable organisation that specialises in food distribution.
vocabulary.exampleAR: عملنا مع منظمة خيرية متخصصة في توزيع الطعام.

vocabulary.definition: to offer to do something without being paid; a person who does this
vocabulary.exampleEN: She volunteers at the centre every Saturday.
vocabulary.exampleAR: هي تتطوع في المركز كل سبت.

vocabulary.definition: practical assistance that involves doing tasks directly rather than giving advice
vocabulary.exampleEN: The programme provides hands-on help, which includes cooking meals and repairing equipment.
vocabulary.exampleAR: البرنامج يقدم مساعدة عملية، والتي تشمل طهي الوجبات وإصلاح الأجهزة.

vocabulary.definition: to take the first step to start something without waiting for instructions
vocabulary.exampleEN: He decided to take initiative and organise a neighbourly food collection.
vocabulary.exampleAR: قرر أن يتخذ المبادرة وينظم حملة جمع طعام بين الجيران.

vocabulary.definition: to register to take part in an activity
vocabulary.exampleEN: If you sign up for the rota, you'll only need to help one morning a month.
vocabulary.exampleAR: إذا سجلت للاشتراك في الجدول، ستحتاج للمساعدة صباحًا واحدًا فقط كل شهر.

vocabulary.definition: the strong effect that something has on a situation or person
vocabulary.exampleEN: The project had an immediate impact on residents' safety.
vocabulary.exampleAR: كان للمشروع تأثير فوري على سلامة السكان.

vocabulary.definition: able to continue over a long period without causing problems
vocabulary.exampleEN: They developed a sustainable plan that uses local volunteers and recycled materials.
vocabulary.exampleAR: طوروا خطة مستدامة تستخدم متطوعين محليين ومواد معاد تدويرها.

grammar.topic: Defining and non-defining relative clauses
grammar.concept: Use defining relative clauses to identify the specific person or thing (no commas). Use non-defining relative clauses to add extra information about someone or something already identified (use commas).
grammar.arabicComparison: الجملة الوصفية المعرفة تُعرّف الشيء أو الشخص وتكون بدون فواصل. الجملة الوصفية غير المعرفة تضيف معلومة إضافية عن شيء معروف مسبقًا ويُكتب بينها فواصل.
grammar.structure: Defining: noun + who/that/which + verb (no commas). Non-defining: noun + , who/which, + verb (with commas).
grammar.commonError: Students often use commas with defining clauses or use 'which' for defining clauses in informal writing. Also avoid omitting the relative pronoun when it is needed for clarity.
grammar.exampleEN:
Defining: The volunteer who speaks Arabic will lead the session.
Non-defining: Mr Ali, who speaks Arabic, will lead the session.
grammar.exampleAR:
تعريفية: المتطوع الذي يتكلم العربية سوف يقود الجلسة.
غير تعريفية: السيد علي، الذي يتكلم العربية، سوف يقود الجلسة.

readingBrief: Read an original 250–350-word interview with the coordinator of a grassroots project that supports isolated older people. The piece should explain how the project started, the practical services it offers, and one success story that shows the project's impact. The interview must include at least three examples of defining or non-defining relative clauses and one quoted opinion from a volunteer.
writingPrompt: Write a formal email (140–180 words) to the local council officer responsible for community services proposing a new volunteer-led initiative that supports elderly residents. State the problem, explain your proposed solution, and request a short meeting. Audience: council officer; Purpose: propose and request support. Success criteria: organise the email into clear paragraphs (problem, proposal, request), use at least two relative clauses (one defining, one non-defining), and keep a polite, formal tone.

title: How a story becomes news

outcome.canDo: I can describe how a story moves from a personal account to published news, evaluate the reliability of sources, and use reporting verbs and source language to write a clear, balanced short report.
outcome.canDoArabic: أستطيع وصف كيف تتحول الحكاية من رواية شخصية إلى خبر منشور، وتقييم موثوقية المصادر، واستخدام أفعال التبليغ ولغة المصدر لكتابة تقرير قصير واضح ومتوازن.
outcome.scenario: You heard a local incident from different people (a neighbour, an eye‑witness, and a social media post). You need to explain to a community newspaper editor whether the story is ready to publish and why.
outcome.scenarioArabic: سمعت عن حادث محلي من عدة أشخاص (جار، شاهِد عيان، ومنشور على وسائل التواصل). عليك أن تشرح لمحرر صحيفة المجتمع إن كان يمكن نشر القصة ولماذا.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Tell briefly about an experience when you heard something important first from one person and later from others. What changed in the story?
retrieval.purpose: Retrieve A2 experience language (past events, simple sequence of actions) and prepare to compare perspectives at B1.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Describe a plan you made recently related to a local service (e.g., arranging help, reporting a problem). Who did you tell and how did they respond?
retrieval.purpose: Repurpose A2 plans and services language to practise reporting what others said.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Say whether you prefer short social posts or formal news when you want reliable information and explain why.
retrieval.purpose: Use A2 preferences and opinions to introduce evaluation language for source reliability.

retrieval.language: Arabic
retrieval.prompt: احكِ عن موقف تغيرت فيه المعلومات عندما سمعته من أكثر من شخص. من قال ماذا؟
retrieval.purpose: استرجاع خبرات (الماضي، الآراء) بلغة بسيطة لتحضير المناقشة عن وجهات النظر وموثوقية المصادر.

priorLevelLinks: A2: talk about past experiences (I went to..., I heard...)
A2: describe plans (I'm going to..., we arranged...)
A2: give opinions and preferences (I think..., I prefer...)
A2: use basic service language (call the police, report a problem)
network.learningNote: At B1, shift from telling a story to reporting it: practise choosing reporting verbs (claim, admit, deny) and adding source language (according to X) to show how reliable information is. Use neutral verbs for facts, stronger verbs only when you can support them.
network.learningNoteArabic: في مستوى B1، انتقل من سرد الحكاية إلى الإبلاغ عنها: تدرب على اختيار أفعال التبليغ (claim, admit, deny) وإضافة لغة المصدر (according to X) لإظهار مدى موثوقية المعلومات. استخدم الأفعال المحايدة للحقائق، والأفعال الأقوى فقط عندما تدعمها أدلة.

wordFamilies.note: Use 'report' as a verb for describing the action (they reported the event) and as a noun for the product (a news report). 'Reporter' is the person.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: استخدم 'report' كفعل لوصف الفعل (they reported the event) وكاسم للمنتج (a news report). 'Reporter' تعني الصحفي.

wordFamilies.note: Common in news contexts: journalists verify facts before publishing. 'Verification' is the process.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: شائع في سياق الأخبار: الصحفيون يَتحققون من الحقائق قبل النشر. 'Verification' تعني عملية التحقق.

wordFamilies.note: Admit often appears in quotes or reports when someone accepts responsibility or confirms a fact.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: يظهر 'admit' غالباً في الاقتباسات أو التقارير عندما يعترف شخص بمسؤولية أو يؤكد حقيقة.

vocabulary.definition: used to show the source of information (who said or wrote something)
vocabulary.exampleEN: According to the neighbour, the alarm went off at midnight.
vocabulary.exampleAR: وفقاً للجار، انفجر إنذار الساعة منتصف الليل.

vocabulary.definition: a person or document known to provide accurate information
vocabulary.exampleEN: The editor spoke to a reliable source inside the council before publishing.
vocabulary.exampleAR: تحدث المحرر إلى مصدر موثوق داخل المجلس قبل النشر.

vocabulary.definition: an account from someone who experienced an event personally
vocabulary.exampleEN: Her first‑hand account of the accident helped the reporter understand the timeline.
vocabulary.exampleAR: ساعدتنا روايتها المباشرة عن الحادث على فهم التسلسل الزمني.

vocabulary.definition: a description of an event by someone who saw it happen
vocabulary.exampleEN: The eye‑witness account contradicted the first social media post.
vocabulary.exampleAR: تعارضت شهادة شاهد العيان مع المنشور الأول على وسائل التواصل.

vocabulary.definition: a piece of information that has not yet been checked for accuracy
vocabulary.exampleEN: Journalists labelled the message an unverified report until they found confirmation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: وصَف الصحفيون الرسالة بأنها تقرير غير مؤكَّد حتى وجدوا تأكيداً.

vocabulary.definition: to say something clearly or officially, often used in reports or news
vocabulary.exampleEN: The mayor stated that emergency services were responding to the flood.
vocabulary.exampleAR: صرّحَ العمدةُ بأنّ خدماتَ الطوارئِ تستجيبُ للفيضانِ.

vocabulary.definition: to state something as a fact when it has not been proven
vocabulary.exampleEN: A group alleged that the contractor ignored safety rules.
vocabulary.exampleAR: زعمت مجموعة أن المقاول أغفل قواعد السلامة.

vocabulary.definition: to accept that something is true, often reluctantly
vocabulary.exampleEN: The company admitted there had been delays.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أقرت الشركة بوجود تأخيرات.

vocabulary.definition: to state that something is not true
vocabulary.exampleEN: The council denied responsibility for the decision.
vocabulary.exampleAR: نفى المجلس مسؤوليته عن القرار.

vocabulary.definition: to check that something is true or accurate
vocabulary.exampleEN: Reporters tried to verify the time of the incident before writing the story.
vocabulary.exampleAR: حاول الصحفيون التحقق من وقت الحادث قبل كتابة القصة.

vocabulary.definition: a tendency to favour one perspective or outcome over others
vocabulary.exampleEN: Readers noticed a bias in the way the article described the protest.
vocabulary.exampleAR: لاحظ القراء وجود تحيّز في طريقة وصف المقال للاحتجاج.

vocabulary.definition: to investigate statements to ensure they are accurate; the process of doing that
vocabulary.exampleEN: Before publishing, the team fact‑checked the main claims.
vocabulary.exampleAR: قبل النشر، قام الفريق بفحص الحقائق المتعلقة بالادعاءات الرئيسية.

grammar.topic: reporting verbs and source language
grammar.concept: Use specific reporting verbs (say, claim, admit, deny, allege) and source phrases (according to, the spokesperson said, a witness reported) to show who provides information and how reliable it is.
grammar.arabicComparison: استخدم أفعال تبليغ محددة وعبارات توضح المصدر (according to, قال المتحدث) لتبيان من يقدّم المعلومة ومدى موثوقيتها.
grammar.structure: Source + reporting verb + (that) + clause. / According to + source + , + clause. / '"Quote,"' + source + said.
grammar.commonError: Mixing direct and indirect reporting incorrectly (e.g., using 'according to that' or wrong verb tense after 'said' when the source is recent). Also over‑using strong verbs (allege, claim) without evidence.
grammar.exampleEN: According to an eye‑witness, the car stopped before the crossing. The witness claimed that the lights were red, but the council denied responsibility.
grammar.exampleAR: وفقاً لشاهد عيان، توقفت السيارة قبل الممر. زعم الشاهد أن الإشارة كانت حمراء، لكن المجلس نفى المسؤولية.

readingBrief: Read an original 250–350‑word feature article titled 'From Garden Gossip to Front Page' that follows one local incident as it spreads: a neighbour's first‑hand account, social media posts, a short interview with a witness, a comment from the council, and an editor's decision about publishing. The article highlights how different sources use different verbs (claimed, admitted, denied), shows where the facts were verified or left unverified, and asks readers to consider reliability and bias. The text contains clear examples of 'according to' and 'a reliable source' and includes small direct quotes and paraphrases.
writingPrompt: Write a 140–180‑word email to the editor of your community newspaper. Purpose: advise whether the recent local story (a reported late‑night disturbance) should be published now, held for more checking, or rejected. Include: a short summary of the different accounts, your evaluation of their reliability, and a clear recommendation. Success criteria: organise your email into a short introduction, two supporting paragraphs (summary + evaluation), and a conclusion with a recommendation; use a neutral, professional tone and at least two reporting verbs or source phrases (for example, 'according to', 'claimed', 'denied').

title: Attention by design

outcome.canDo: I can explain how app features cause habits and argue for design changes using cause, effect and emphasis language.
outcome.canDoArabic: أستطيع شرح كيف تتسبب ميزات التطبيقات في تشكيل عادات وأقترح تغييرات تصميمية مستعملاً تعابير السببية والنتيجة والتوكيد.
outcome.scenario: You are a community learning coordinator. Students complain that the university app distracts them during study time. Write a short proposal that explains the problem (cause and effect), evaluates two possible solutions, and recommends one with reasons.
outcome.scenarioArabic: أنت منسق برامج تعلم مجتمعي. يشتكي الطلاب من أن تطبيق الجامعة يشتت انتباههم أثناء وقت الدراسة. اكتب مقترحًا قصيرًا يشرح المشكلة (السبب والنتيجة)، يقيم حلّين محتملين، ويوصي بحل واحد مع الأسباب.

retrieval.language: experiences
retrieval.prompt: Think of a recent time you felt distracted by a phone app. Describe briefly what happened and how it affected your study or work.
retrieval.purpose: Recycle A2 talk-about-experience language while preparing students to build a linked narrative of cause and effect at B1.

retrieval.language: plans
retrieval.prompt: Say what you plan to change in your phone settings this week to reduce distractions (e.g., mute notifications, uninstall an app).
retrieval.purpose: Use simple future/intent language from A2 but extend to explain reasons and expected effects.

retrieval.language: preferences
retrieval.prompt: Say which notification type you prefer (sound, vibration, none) and why in one or two sentences.
retrieval.purpose: Start from A2 preference statements and develop short justifications showing cause → effect.

retrieval.language: services
retrieval.prompt: Recall a service (library, classroom booking, or counselling) you used when distracted. Describe how the service helped in one or two sentences.
retrieval.purpose: Connect A2 descriptions of services to evaluating solutions at B1 level.

network.learningNote: Focus on linking cause and effect with clear connectors (because, so, therefore, as a result) and add emphasis with words like particularly and especially; prefer natural multi-word chunks used in tech discussions (e.g., 'push notification', 'time well spent').
network.learningNoteArabic: ركز على ربط السبب والنتيجة بواسطة أدوات الربط (because، so، therefore، as a result) وإضافة التوكيد بكلمات مثل particularly وespecially؛ استخدم عبارات متعددة الكلمات الشائعة في سياق التكنولوجيا (مثل 'push notification'، 'time well spent').

wordFamilies.note: Common collocations: pay attention, capture attention, sustain attention.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: تراكيب شائعة: pay attention (ينتبه)، capture attention (يجذب الانتباه)، sustain attention (يحافظ على الانتباه).

wordFamilies.note: Use persuasive/adverbs to describe techniques; persuasion can be neutral or negative depending on context.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: استخدم صفات/حال لتوصيف تقنيات الإقناع؛ يمكن أن تكون persuasion محايدة أو سلبية حسب السياق.

wordFamilies.note: Engage/engagement often describe user behaviour; disengage is the opposite.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: engage/engagement تصف سلوك المستخدم؛ disengage تعني الانفصال أو فقدان الاهتمام.

vocabulary.definition: to get someone's focus quickly
vocabulary.exampleEN: Short videos often capture attention more quickly than long texts.
vocabulary.exampleAR: غالبًا ما تجذب الفيديوهات القصيرة الانتباه بسرعة أكثر من النصوص الطويلة.

vocabulary.definition: to keep someone's focus for a period of time
vocabulary.exampleEN: Teachers try to sustain attention with varied activities.
vocabulary.exampleAR: يحاول المدرسون الحفاظ على الانتباه بأنشطة متنوعة.

vocabulary.definition: a message sent by an app to a user's device to get attention
vocabulary.exampleEN: Too many push notifications can interrupt study sessions.
vocabulary.exampleAR: عدد كبير من الإشعارات المنبثقة قد يقطع جلسات الدراسة.

vocabulary.definition: to gently encourage a person to do something (often by small design choices)
vocabulary.exampleEN: The app nudges users to open it by showing a red dot.
vocabulary.exampleAR: يدفع التطبيق المستخدمين لفتحه عبر إظهار نقطة حمراء.

vocabulary.definition: describes a product or action that encourages repeated use until it becomes a habit
vocabulary.exampleEN: Many social apps use habit-forming features to increase daily use.
vocabulary.exampleAR: تستخدم العديد من التطبيقات الاجتماعية ميزات تُكوّن العادات لزيادة الاستخدام اليومي.

vocabulary.definition: activities considered valuable or worthwhile for a person's time
vocabulary.exampleEN: Designers argue about what counts as time well spent on an app.
vocabulary.exampleAR: يتجادل المصممون حول ما يعتبر وقتًا مستغلاً جيدًا في التطبيق.

vocabulary.definition: agreeing to receive a service or feature (e.g., notifications) rather than being subscribed by default
vocabulary.exampleEN: Make notifications opt-in so users choose what they receive.
vocabulary.exampleAR: اجعل الإشعارات بنظام opt-in حتى يختار المستخدمون ما يتلقونه.

vocabulary.definition: the act of convincing someone to do or believe something
vocabulary.exampleEN: Marketing teams study persuasion techniques carefully.
vocabulary.exampleAR: تدرس فرق التسويق تقنيات الإقناع بعناية.

vocabulary.definition: the level of a user's involvement or interaction with a product
vocabulary.exampleEN: Higher user engagement usually means users spend more time in an app.
vocabulary.exampleAR: عادةً ما يعني ارتفاع تفاعل المستخدم أن المستخدمين يقضون وقتًا أطول في التطبيق.

vocabulary.definition: the idea that human attention is a scarce resource companies compete for
vocabulary.exampleEN: In the attention economy, companies design features to win users' focus.
vocabulary.exampleAR: في اقتصاد الانتباه، تصمم الشركات ميزات لكسب تركيز المستخدمين.

vocabulary.definition: using technology intentionally and with awareness of effects
vocabulary.exampleEN: Encouraging mindful use can reduce compulsive checking of apps.
vocabulary.exampleAR: تشجيع الاستخدام الواعي يمكن أن يقلل من التحقق القهري من التطبيقات.

vocabulary.definition: to create interfaces or features that intentionally attract user focus
vocabulary.exampleEN: Some teams openly design for attention while others avoid dark patterns.
vocabulary.exampleAR: بعض الفرق تصمم صراحة لجذب الانتباه بينما يتجنب آخرون الأنماط المضللة.

grammar.topic: cause, effect, and emphasis
grammar.concept: Use linking words to show cause and effect (because, since, due to, therefore, as a result) and words/structures to add emphasis (especially, in particular, It is X that...).
grammar.arabicComparison: استخدم أدوات الربط لاظهار السبب والنتيجة (because، since، due to، therefore، as a result) وكلمات/تراكيب للتوكيد (especially، in particular، It is X that...).
grammar.structure: Cause: because / since / due to + noun/clause. Effect: therefore / so / as a result + clause. Emphasis: especially / particularly + noun/phrase; It is + X + that + clause for focus.
grammar.commonError: Mixing 'because of' with a full clause (use 'because' for clauses) or overusing 'so' without clear cause-effect links.
grammar.exampleEN: Because students received constant push notifications, their study time decreased; as a result, many asked for an opt-in system. It is the notifications, especially the sounds, that interrupt focus.
grammar.exampleAR: لأن الطلاب تلقوا إشعارات منبثقة مستمرة، قلّ وقت دراستهم؛ ونتيجة لذلك، طلب الكثيرون نظام opt-in. إن الإشعارات، وخصوصًا الأصوات، هي التي تقطع التركيز.

readingBrief: A 250–350-word interview with a product designer who reduced notifications in a study-aid app. The designer explains the causes of distraction, evaluates two redesign choices (opt-in notifications vs scheduled summary), and reflects on ethical responsibilities and measurable effects on users' study time.
writingPrompt: Write a 140–180-word formal proposal email to the university app team (audience: app developers and student services). Purpose: explain the problem (cause and effect), compare two solutions, and recommend one. Success criteria: organise into three clear paragraphs (problem, solutions with brief evaluation, recommendation) and use a respectful, professional tone; include at least three cause-effect connectors (e.g., because, therefore, as a result).

title: Buying an idea

outcome.canDo: I can present and defend a short advertising idea using comparatives, qualifiers and persuasive language.
outcome.canDoArabic: أستطيع عرض ودعم فكرة إعلان قصيرة باستخدام المقارنات، أدوات التقييد ولغة الإقناع.
outcome.scenario: You need to persuade a local community centre committee to approve a small budget for a short advert or poster campaign. You must explain the idea, compare it with alternatives, and use qualifiers and evidence to make a convincing, realistic case.
outcome.scenarioArabic: تحتاج لإقناع لجنة المركز المجتمعي المحلي بالموافقة على ميزانية صغيرة لحملة إعلان قصيرة أو ملصقات. يجب أن تشرح الفكرة، تقارنها بالبدائل، وتستخدم أدوات تقييد وأدلة لتقديم قضية مقنعة وواقعية.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Remember a time you used or paid for a service (A2: experience). Briefly note what you liked, what you didn’t, and one change you would make.
retrieval.purpose: Activate experience vocabulary to create specific examples you can use as evidence in a persuasive pitch.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Think of a plan you have (A2: plans). Outline the plan in two sentences and one reason it is better than another option.
retrieval.purpose: Repurpose simple planning language to practise quick comparative statements for a persuasive argument.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Say which of two local services you prefer and why (A2: preferences & services). Add one qualifier (e.g., slightly, considerably) to weaken or strengthen your opinion.
retrieval.purpose: Build qualified opinions suitable for B1 persuasive language and for comparing alternatives in a pitch.

priorLevelLinks: A2 experiences: I went to / I liked / I didn't like
A2 plans: I'm going to / I will
A2 preferences: I prefer / I like
A2 services: the service was / it costs
A2 opinions: I think / I believe
A2 change: we changed / we improved
network.learningNote: Focus on teaching comparatives for advantage (more, less, better), qualifiers to make claims realistic (slightly, arguably, possibly, considerably), and persuasive linking language (because, therefore, as a result). Use short model pitches showing one clear recommendation with two supporting reasons and evidence.
network.learningNoteArabic: ركز على تعليم المقارنات لعرض الميزة (أكثر، أقل، أفضل)، وأدوات التقييد لجعل الادعاءات واقعية (قليلاً، من المحتمل، ربما، إلى حد كبير)، ولغة الربط الإقناعية (لأن، لذلك، نتيجة لذلك). استخدم نماذج عرض قصيرة مع توصية واضحة ودعم بحجتين ودليل.

wordFamilies.note: Use as a noun for statements and as a verb for asserting facts; remember to back up strong claims with evidence.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: تستخدم كاسم للدلالة على بيان وكفعل للاصرار على شيء؛ يجب دعم الادعاءات القوية بأدلة.

wordFamilies.note: persuade (verb) and persuasive (adj) are key in pitches; persuasion (noun) names the process.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: persuade فعل وpersuasive صفة مهمان في العروض؛ persuasion اسم للعملية.

wordFamilies.note: Value refers to benefit or worth — useful in phrases like 'value for money' or 'valuable feedback'.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: value تشير إلى الفائدة أو القيمة — مفيدة في عبارات مثل 'قيمة مقابل المال' أو 'تعليقات قيّمة'.

vocabulary.definition: A short, persuasive presentation explaining why someone should buy or support a product, service, or idea.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Her sales pitch made the service seem more reliable than competitors'.
vocabulary.exampleAR: سلط عرضها الترويجي الضوء على أن الخدمة أكثر موثوقية من خدمات المنافسين.

vocabulary.definition: To state something as true, especially in advertising or argument.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Before you make a claim about results, show customer feedback.
vocabulary.exampleAR: قبل أن تقدّم ادعاءً عن النتائج، أظهر تعليقات العملاء.

vocabulary.definition: To provide evidence or reasons that make a claim believable.
vocabulary.exampleEN: We can back up that claim with three testimonials.
vocabulary.exampleAR: يمكننا دعم ذلك الادعاء بثلاث شهادات.

vocabulary.definition: The benefit received compared to the amount spent.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Families say the course offers good value for money.
vocabulary.exampleAR: تقول العائلات إن الدورة تقدم قيمة جيدة مقابل المال.

vocabulary.definition: A visual look that quickly attracts attention.
vocabulary.exampleEN: An eye-catching design will help posters stand out on the street.
vocabulary.exampleAR: التصميم اللافت سيساعد الملصقات على البروز في الشارع.

vocabulary.definition: The particular group of people an advertisement is aimed at.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Our target audience is local young parents and carers.
vocabulary.exampleAR: جمهورنا المستهدف هم الآباء الشباب ومقدمو الرعاية المحليون.

vocabulary.definition: Opinions and responses from customers about a product or service.
vocabulary.exampleEN: We used customer feedback to improve the workshop timetable.
vocabulary.exampleAR: استخدمنا تعليقات العملاء لتحسين جدول الورش.

vocabulary.definition: Able to convince someone to believe or do something.
vocabulary.exampleEN: A short, persuasive message can increase attendance.
vocabulary.exampleAR: رسالة قصيرة ومقنعة قد تزيد الحضور.

vocabulary.definition: A word or phrase (e.g., slightly, probably) that makes a statement less absolute.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Use qualifiers like 'arguably' or 'slightly' to avoid overstatement.
vocabulary.exampleAR: استخدم أدوات تقييد مثل 'من المحتمل' أو 'قليلاً' لتجنب المبالغة.

vocabulary.definition: An aspect that makes something better than an alternative.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Our comparative advantage is a lower cost and local delivery.
vocabulary.exampleAR: ميزتنا النسبية هي التكلفة الأقل والتوصيل المحلي.

vocabulary.definition: Providing good results for the amount of money spent.
vocabulary.exampleEN: A short poster campaign is a cost-effective way to reach people.
vocabulary.exampleAR: حملة ملصقات قصيرة هي طريقة فعّالة من حيث التكلفة للوصول إلى الناس.

vocabulary.definition: To describe something as better or worse than it really is.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Advertisers must avoid exaggerating claims without proof.
vocabulary.exampleAR: يجب على المعلنين تجنب المبالغة في الادعاءات بدون دليل.

grammar.topic: comparatives, qualifiers, and persuasive language
grammar.concept: Use comparatives to show advantages (more, less, better), qualifiers to make claims realistic (slightly, arguably, probably), and persuasive linking language to structure reasons and evidence.
grammar.arabicComparison: في العربية نستخدم 'أكثر' أو '-أ/-ة' للمقارنة؛ في الإنجليزية القاعدة الشائعة هي 'more + adjective' أو adjective + -er، وأدوات التقييد تُستخدم لتليين الادعاء.
grammar.structure: Comparatives: X is more/less + adjective + than Y; Qualifiers: (arguably / slightly / probably / considerably) + clause; Persuasive linkers: Because / Therefore / As a result / For example / Evidence shows that ...
grammar.commonError: Using absolute statements without evidence (e.g., 'the best' without proof) or overusing comparatives without clear reference (forgetting 'than' or the second item).
grammar.exampleEN: Our course is more accessible than the city alternative, but it is slightly more expensive. Because customer feedback shows better outcomes locally, we recommend a pilot campaign.
grammar.exampleAR: دورتنا أكثر إمكانية للوصول من البديل في المدينة، لكنها أغلى قليلاً. لأن تعليقات العملاء تُظهر نتائج أفضل محلياً، نوصي بحملة تجريبية.

readingBrief: Read an original 250–350-word interview with a small café owner who used customer feedback to change the menu and launch a short poster campaign. The interview should describe the initial problem, the alternative promotional options considered (social media posts, leaflets, posters), why the owner chose an inexpensive poster design, and how they used qualifiers and comparatives when discussing results (e.g., 'more customers', 'slightly higher cost', 'arguably better engagement'). Focus on identifying persuasive phrases, qualifiers, and two comparative statements the owner uses as evidence.
writingPrompt: Write a 140–180-word pitch to the community centre committee proposing a short poster campaign (audience: community centre committee; purpose: to persuade them to approve a small budget). Organise your text with a clear opening sentence stating your idea, one paragraph with two comparative reasons why this option is better than an alternative, and one short paragraph with evidence or customer feedback and a polite request to approve funding. Tone: professional but friendly. Success criterion: your pitch must include at least two comparatives, one qualifier, and a clear organisational structure (opening idea, reasons, evidence, conclusion).

title: What the data does not say

outcome.canDo: I can describe what data shows and what it does not prove, using modal deduction and cautious language to make qualified claims.
outcome.canDoArabic: أستطيع وصف ما تظهره البيانات وما لا تثبته، باستخدام أساليب الاستدلال الاحتمالى ولغة متحفظة لتقديم ادعاءات مؤهلة.
outcome.scenario: You are preparing a short briefing for a neighbourhood group about a recent community survey on public transport. You must summarise clear findings, point out limitations, and suggest cautious next steps.
outcome.scenarioArabic: أنت تُعد ملخصًا قصيرًا لمجموعة الحي حول استبيان مجتمعي حديث عن وسائل النقل العامة. يجب أن تلخّص النتائج الواضحة، تشير إلى القيود، وتقترح خطوات لاحقة متحفظة.

retrieval.language: experiences
retrieval.prompt: Briefly describe one experience you had with a local service (e.g., bus, GP, shop). Then say what that single experience might suggest about the overall service. Use one modal of possibility (might/could).
retrieval.purpose: Reactivate A2 experience language while practising cautious deduction.

retrieval.language: plans
retrieval.prompt: Tell the class about a plan you made recently (travel, study, work). Then explain how the outcome of that plan could change your future plans, using should or might.
retrieval.purpose: Use A2 plan vocabulary and practise making tentative predictions.

retrieval.language: preferences
retrieval.prompt: State a simple preference (I prefer X to Y) and then infer why you might prefer it, using because + a modal (might/could) to describe uncertainty.
retrieval.purpose: Link A2 preference language with cautious reasoning.

retrieval.language: services
retrieval.prompt: Describe a service you used (e.g., a delivery, repair). Summarise one piece of evidence from that service and say what it may — and may not — prove about the whole company.
retrieval.purpose: Repurpose A2 service vocabulary for a B1 evaluation task.

network.anchor: What the data does and does not show
chunks: take with a grain of salt
network.learningNote: At B1 we move from reporting facts to qualifying claims. Teach modals of deduction (may/might/could/must/can't) and perfect modals for past events (must have, could have). Encourage students to pair clear evidence language (based on the data, the survey shows) with cautious verbs and hedges (might, appear to, seem to) rather than absolute statements.
network.learningNoteArabic: في مستوى B1 ننتقل من سرد الوقائع إلى تأهيل الادعاءات. علّم صيغ الأفعال المساعدة للاستدلال (may/might/could/must/can't) وصيغ الماضي (must have, could have). شجِّع الطلبة على مزج عبارات الأدلة الواضحة (بناءً على البيانات، يظهر الاستبيان) مع أفعال ومصطلحات تحفظ (قد، يبدو أن) بدلًا من جمل حاسمة.

wordFamilies.note: Use 'infer' to mean draw a conclusion; 'inference' is the noun for that result.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: استخدم 'infer' بمعنى استنتاج؛ و'inference' الاسم الذي يدلّ على نتيجة الاستنتاج.

wordFamilies.note: Misleading describes information that gives the wrong impression.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: misleading تصف المعلومات التي تعطي انطباعًا خاطئًا.

wordFamilies.note: Plausible is useful when a claim is reasonable but not certain.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: plausible تعني أن الادعاء معقول لكنه ليس مؤكدًا.

vocabulary.definition: to make a judgement based on the available evidence
vocabulary.exampleEN: We can draw a conclusion that most patients are satisfied, but the sample is small.
vocabulary.exampleAR: يمكننا استخلاص استنتاج بأن معظم المرضى راضون، لكن العينة صغيرة.

vocabulary.definition: when an interpretation or decision is guided by the collected information
vocabulary.exampleEN: Based on the data, bus delays are more common in the mornings.
vocabulary.exampleAR: بناءً على البيانات، تأخيرات الحافلات أكثر شيوعًا في الصباح.

vocabulary.arabic: يأخذ في الحسبان / يضع في الاعتبار
vocabulary.definition: to consider or make provision for something when planning or judging
vocabulary.exampleEN: When interpreting the survey, we should allow for possible sampling errors.
vocabulary.exampleAR: عند تفسير نتائج الاستطلاع، يجب أن نأخذ في الحسبان احتمال وجود أخطاء في العينة.

vocabulary.definition: indicates a possibility, not a certainty
vocabulary.exampleEN: There is a chance the problem will resolve itself, but we shouldn't rely on that.
vocabulary.exampleAR: هناك احتمال أن تحل المشكلة ذاتيًا، لكن لا ينبغي أن نعتمد على ذلك.

vocabulary.definition: a clear statistical link between two variables, not necessarily causal
vocabulary.exampleEN: The data shows a strong correlation between hours studied and test scores.
vocabulary.exampleAR: تُظهر البيانات ارتباطًا قويًا بين ساعات الدراسة ودرجات الاختبار.

vocabulary.definition: not providing a clear result or decision
vocabulary.exampleEN: The results are inconclusive because the response rate was low.
vocabulary.exampleAR: النتائج غير حاسمة لأن معدل الاستجابة كان منخفضًا.

vocabulary.definition: a range within which the true value is expected to lie, accounting for sampling variation
vocabulary.exampleEN: With a 5% margin of error, the true support level could be higher or lower.
vocabulary.exampleAR: مع هامش خطأ قدره ٥٪، قد تكون نسبة التأييد الحقيقية أعلى أو أقل.

vocabulary.definition: giving the wrong idea or impression
vocabulary.exampleEN: A single dramatic story can be misleading when it is taken as typical.
vocabulary.exampleAR: قصة درامية واحدة قد تكون مضللة إذا اعتُبرت نموذجًا عامًا.

vocabulary.definition: seeming reasonable or likely, but not certain
vocabulary.exampleEN: One plausible explanation is that fewer people answered due to bad weather.
vocabulary.exampleAR: تفسير محتمل هو أن قلة الإجابات بسبب سوء الطقس.

vocabulary.definition: to conclude information from evidence and reasoning rather than from explicit statements
vocabulary.exampleEN: From these numbers we can infer that demand has fallen slightly.
vocabulary.exampleAR: من هذه الأرقام يمكننا استنتاج أن الطلب انخفض قليلاً.

vocabulary.word: take with a grain of salt
vocabulary.definition: to view something with scepticism or not to accept it completely
vocabulary.exampleEN: Take the headline with a grain of salt — the full report gives a different picture.
vocabulary.exampleAR: تلقَّ العنوان بتحفّظ — فالتقرير الكامل يعطي صورة مختلفة.

vocabulary.definition: a general direction in which something is changing or developing
vocabulary.exampleEN: The trend over the past five years suggests gradual improvement.
vocabulary.exampleAR: تشير الاتجاهات خلال السنوات الخمس الماضية إلى تحسّن تدريجي.

grammar.topic: modal deduction and cautious claims
grammar.concept: Use modal verbs (must, might, could, may, can't) and perfect modals (must have, might have, could have) to state degrees of certainty about present or past facts; combine with hedging phrases (appear to, seem to, suggest) for cautious claims.
grammar.arabicComparison: استخدم الأفعال المساعدة للدلالة على درجات اليقين عن الحاضر أو الماضي؛ وادمجها مع عبارات التحفظ (يبدو أن، يشير إلى) لتقديم ادعاءات متحفظة.
grammar.structure: Present deduction: modal + base verb (e.g., 'This must be an error.' / 'They might agree.'). Past deduction: modal + have + past participle (e.g., 'They must have missed it.' / 'She could have misunderstood.'). Hedging: phrase + that + clause (e.g., 'The data suggests that...').
grammar.commonError: Students often use 'must' when they mean 'might' (overstating certainty), or mix up perfect modals (e.g., *'might be' for past deductions instead of 'might have been').
grammar.exampleEN: The survey results might reflect short-term problems; they must not be taken as a definitive judgment of the whole service.
grammar.exampleAR: قد تعكس نتائج الاستبيان مشكلات مؤقتة؛ ولا يجب أن تُعتبر حكمًا قاطعًا على الخدمة ككل.

readingBrief: Read an original 250–350-word investigative article for a local newsletter. The article reports the results of a short community survey on weekday bus reliability. It highlights a clear increase in morning delays (data and percentages), notes a low response rate from certain neighbourhoods, and quotes two residents with opposing views. The piece should present facts (times, percentages), raise questions about sample size and possible bias, and model cautious language (may/might/could, appear to, suggest) rather than absolute claims. Students will use the article to practise distinguishing clear evidence from plausible inference.
writingPrompt: Write a 140–180-word formal email to the neighbourhood group summarising what the community survey does and does not show about bus reliability. Audience: neighbourhood group and local councillor. Purpose: report findings, point out limitations, and recommend one cautious next step. Success criteria: organise the email with a brief opening statement, one paragraph summarising clear results (use specific data language), one paragraph outlining limitations and uncertainty (use modals for deduction), and a final recommended action; maintain a polite, cautious formal tone.

title: Culture in everyday choices

outcome.canDo: I can explain how culture influences everyday choices, using contrast and concession to make respectful generalisations.
outcome.canDoArabic: أستطيع شرح كيف تؤثر الثقافة في الخيارات اليومية، مع استخدام المقارنة والتنازل لصياغة تعميمات محترمة.
outcome.scenario: You are writing a short piece for a local community newsletter about one everyday custom from your background. You must explain why you follow it, mention at least one example of someone choosing differently, and use contrast or concession to avoid stereotyping.
outcome.scenarioArabic: أنت تكتب فقرة قصيرة لنشرة مجتمعية محلية عن عادة يومية من خلفيتك. يجب أن تشرح لماذا تتبعها، تذكر مثالاً لشخص يختار بطريقة مختلفة، وتستخدم المقارنة أو جملة التنازل لتجنب التعميمات النمطية.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Think of a personal experience when culture affected a choice you made (food, dress, greeting, service). In 3–4 sentences: 1) say what happened, 2) say what you planned or expected, 3) give your preference and one opinion about why people act differently.
retrieval.purpose: Repurpose A2 experiences, plans, preferences and opinions into a short narrative that prepares you to contrast and concede differences.

retrieval.language: Arabic
retrieval.prompt: تذكّر موقفاً حدث معك حيث أثّرت الثقافة في خيار يومي (مثل الطعام أو اللبس أو التحية أو خدمة). اكتب ٣–٤ جمل: ١) ماذا حدث، ٢) ماذا كنت تخطط أو تتوقع، ٣) ما تفضيلك ورأيك عن سبب اختلاف الناس.
retrieval.purpose: إعادة استخدام مفردات A2 (تجارب، خطط، تفضيلات، آراء) ولكن بمهمّة تتطلب ربط الأحداث مع التباين أو التنازل.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Describe a small change you made recently (e.g., tried a different greeting or food) and one service or habit you would keep. Use one concessive phrase (e.g., although, despite) and one contrasting phrase (e.g., while) in 3–5 sentences.
retrieval.purpose: Turn an A2 idea of change and services into a concise B1 task that practices contrast and concession.

network.learningNote: At B1 learners should use contrast (while, whereas) and concession (although, despite) to give balanced, respectful generalisations. Avoid absolute language (always, never). Practice short contrastive statements before longer explanations.
network.learningNoteArabic: يجب على متعلّمي B1 استخدام أدوات المقارنة (while, whereas) وجمل التنازل (although, despite) لصياغة تعميمات متوازنة ومحترمة. تجنّب عبارات القطع (always, never). تمرّن على جمل مقارنة قصيرة قبل الشرح الأطول.

wordFamilies.note: Adapt relates to changing behaviour to fit a situation (useful when talking about change or compromise).
wordFamilies.noteArabic: يعنى adapt التغيّر أو التكيّف ليتناسب مع موقف معيّن (مفيد عند التحدّث عن التغيير أو التسوية).

wordFamilies.note: Belong and belonging speak about feelings of fitting in or being part of a group.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: belong و belonging تتعلّقان بشعور الانتماء أو الملاءمة داخل مجموعة.

wordFamilies.note: Use choose/choice to discuss preferences; choosy is informal and describes someone selective.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: استخدم choose/choice للحديث عن التفضيلات؛ choosy غير رسمي ويصف شخصاً انتقائياً.

vocabulary.definition: the sense of belonging to a particular culture or group
vocabulary.exampleEN: Her cultural identity includes both family traditions and language.
vocabulary.exampleAR: تتضمن هويتها الثقافية التقاليد العائلية واللغة.

vocabulary.definition: the culture someone was raised in or feels connected to
vocabulary.exampleEN: Students in the class come from many different cultural backgrounds.
vocabulary.exampleAR: الطلاب في الصف يأتون من خلفيات ثقافية متعددة.

vocabulary.definition: existing for a long time and strongly established
vocabulary.exampleEN: The ritual is deeply rooted in the town’s history.
vocabulary.exampleAR: الطقوس متجذرة بعمق في تاريخ المدينة.

vocabulary.definition: an individual choice based on taste or comfort
vocabulary.exampleEN: Wearing bright colours is a personal preference for some people.
vocabulary.exampleAR: ارتداء الألوان الزاهية تفضيل شخصي لدى بعض الأشخاص.

vocabulary.definition: to be accepted or feel comfortable in a group
vocabulary.exampleEN: He changed his hairstyle to fit in at the new school.
vocabulary.exampleAR: غيّر قصة شعره ليندمج في المدرسة الجديدة.

vocabulary.definition: to be noticeably different from others
vocabulary.exampleEN: Her colourful scarf made her stand out at the meeting.
vocabulary.exampleAR: جعَلها وشاحها الملون تبرز في الاجتماع.

vocabulary.definition: to match others in appearance or behaviour so you are not noticed
vocabulary.exampleEN: In the new city she chose simple clothes to blend in.
vocabulary.exampleAR: في المدينة الجديدة اختارت ملابس بسيطة لتندمج.

vocabulary.definition: to behave politely or honour cultural norms
vocabulary.exampleEN: It’s polite to show respect for elders by listening carefully.
vocabulary.exampleAR: من اللائق إظهار الاحترام للكبار بالاستماع بعناية.

vocabulary.definition: to accept and celebrate differences among people of different backgrounds or cultures
vocabulary.exampleEN: In multicultural schools, teachers should embrace diversity to help every student feel included.
vocabulary.exampleAR: في المدارس متعددة الثقافات، يجب على المعلمين احتضان التنوع لمساعدة كل طالب على الشعور بالانتماء.

vocabulary.definition: to change behaviour to fit new conditions or customs
vocabulary.exampleEN: When he moved abroad, he adapted his morning routine to local times.
vocabulary.exampleAR: عند انتقاله للخارج، تكيف مع روتينه الصباحي بحسب الأوقات المحلية.

vocabulary.definition: a fixed, oversimplified idea about a group of people
vocabulary.exampleEN: Avoid using stereotypes; they ignore individual differences.
vocabulary.exampleAR: تجنّب استخدام الصور النمطية؛ فهي تتجاهل الفروق الفردية.

vocabulary.definition: a broad statement that applies to many people or situations (may be useful but risky)
vocabulary.exampleEN: A respectful generalisation might say: ‘Many people prefer…’, not ‘Everyone always…’.
vocabulary.exampleAR: قد يقول التعميم المُحترم: «يفضل الكثيرون…»، لا «الجميع دائماً…».

grammar.topic: contrast, concession, and respectful generalisation
grammar.concept: Use contrast (while, whereas) and concession (although, despite) to compare behaviours and make balanced, cautious generalisations.
grammar.arabicComparison: استخدم أدوات المقارنة (while, whereas) وجمل التنازل (although, despite) للمقارنة بين السلوكيات وصياغة تعميمات متوازنة وحذرة.
grammar.structure: Contrast: 'While X, Y...' / 'Whereas X, Y...'. Concession: 'Although + clause' / 'Despite + noun/gerund'. Respectful generalisation: 'Many people tend to ...', 'Generally speaking, ...', 'Some people prefer ...'.
grammar.commonError: Using absolutes (always/never) or one-word generalisations without qualifiers: e.g., 'All X are Y.' Instead use 'Many'/'Some' and include a concessive clause if needed.
grammar.exampleEN: Although many families eat at home, some prefer eating out; while younger people may try new foods, older generations often keep traditional meals.
grammar.exampleAR: على الرغم من أنّ العديد من العائلات تتناول الطعام في المنزل، إلا أن بعضهم يفضّلون الخروج لتناول الطعام؛ بينما قد يجرب الشباب أطعمة جديدة، غالباً ما يحافظ كبار السن على الوجبات التقليدية.

readingBrief: Read an original 250–350-word interview with a local market vendor who explains three everyday choices shaped by culture (food, dress, greeting). The interview should include: a short personal story, at least one contrasted example of someone choosing differently, and two concessive sentences that soften general statements. Focus: identity, belonging and respectful generalisation.
writingPrompt: Write a 140–180-word email to your community newsletter explaining one everyday custom from your cultural background. Purpose: inform readers why the custom matters to you and acknowledge others may choose differently. Audience: local community members. Success criteria: 1) Organise into two short paragraphs (paragraph 1: description and personal reason; paragraph 2: contrast or concession and a respectful generalisation). 2) Use at least one contrastive phrase (while/whereas) and one concessive structure (although/despite). Maintain a respectful, inclusive tone.

title: A review with a point of view

outcome.canDo: I can write a short, organised review of a book, film or experience that gives clear opinions, supports them with examples, and ends with a recommendation.
outcome.canDoArabic: أستطيع كتابة مراجعة قصيرة منظمة لكتاب أو فيلم أو تجربة، أبدي فيها رأياً واضحاً وأدعمه بأمثلة وأنهي بتوصية.
outcome.scenario: You have been asked to write a short review for your student magazine about a recent film or book. Readers want to know what you liked and didn't like, why, and whether they should see or read it.
outcome.scenarioArabic: طُلب منك كتابة مراجعة قصيرة لمجلة الطلبة عن فيلم أو كتاب حديث. القراء يريدون أن يعرفوا ما أعجبك وما لم يعجبك ولماذا، وهل تنصحهم بمشاهدته أو قراءته.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Think of two recent experiences (A2 language). Write one simple past sentence for each (e.g. I watched a film last weekend). Then change each into a short review sentence that says whether the experience was positive or negative and why.
retrieval.purpose: Activate simple factual language and move from description to evaluation.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Write one A2 sentence about a plan (e.g. I'm going to see a new film). Now rewrite it as a B1 recommendation: mention who would enjoy it and why.
retrieval.purpose: Turn intentions/plans into advice for others.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Write two A2 sentences about preferences (I like comedies; I prefer action). Then expand each into a B1 opinion using an evaluative adjective and a specific reason.
retrieval.purpose: Move from simple likes/dislikes to justified opinions.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Describe one service you used in one A2 sentence (e.g. I used a streaming service). Then explain in B1 how the service quality affected your view of the film/book (positive or negative).
retrieval.purpose: Connect practical details about services to overall evaluation.

priorLevelLinks: A2: experiences — simple past to say what happened
A2: plans — going to / will for intentions
A2: services — describe using simple sentences
A2: opinions — I think / I like
A2: change — talking about past vs present tastes
network.learningNote: At B1 you should combine evaluative adjectives (compelling, predictable, underwhelming) with brief evidence. Use recommendation language (I would recommend, It's worth) and give a reason or audience so your point of view is useful.
network.learningNoteArabic: في مستوى B1 اجمع بين الصفات التقييمية (مثير، متوقع، مخيّب للآمال) ومعها دليل قصير. استخدم عبارات التوصية (أنصح بـ، يستحق) واذكر سبباً أو نوع الجمهور حتى تكون وجهة نظرك مفيدة.

wordFamilies.note: Use 'recommend' with a person or general audience: I highly recommend this film to anyone who likes action.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: تستخدم 'recommend' مع شخص أو جمهور عام: أنصح بشدة بهذا الفيلم لأي شخص يحب الحركة.

wordFamilies.note: Differentiate a critic (person) from critical (adjective) and criticism (noun).
wordFamilies.noteArabic: ميّز بين 'critic' (ناقد) و'critical' (نقدي/حاسم) و'criticism' (نقد).

wordFamilies.note: Use 'performance' for actors' work; 'perform' for the action.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: استخدم 'performance' لعمل الممثلين، و'perform' للفعل نفسه.

vocabulary.definition: A recommendation phrase meaning the film or show has enough quality or interest to spend time watching.
vocabulary.exampleEN: The documentary is well worth watching if you want a clear explanation of the topic.
vocabulary.exampleAR: الفيلم الوثائقي جدير بالمشاهدة إذا أردت شرحاً واضحاً للموضوع.

vocabulary.definition: To give strong positive advice that others should try or see something.
vocabulary.exampleEN: I highly recommend the book for anyone learning about modern history.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أوصي بشدة بهذا الكتاب لأي شخص يتعلم عن التاريخ الحديث.

vocabulary.definition: To fail to achieve what was intended or expected.
vocabulary.exampleEN: The sequel missed the mark because it copied the old plot without fresh ideas.
vocabulary.exampleAR: الجزء الثاني أخطأ الهدف لأنه كرر الحبكة القديمة دون أفكار جديدة.

vocabulary.definition: Having both positive and negative reactions to the same book, film or experience.
vocabulary.exampleEN: I had mixed feelings about the ending: it was clever but left questions unanswered.
vocabulary.exampleAR: كانت لديّ مشاعر مختلطة حيال النهاية: كانت ذكية لكنها تركت أسئلة بلا إجابة.

vocabulary.definition: An especially impressive acting display that attracts attention.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Her stand-out performance made the whole film memorable.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أداؤها البارز جعل الفيلم كله قابلاً للتذكر.

vocabulary.arabic: التواء في الحبكة / مفاجأة في القصة
vocabulary.definition: An unexpected change or revelation in the story that surprises the audience.
vocabulary.exampleEN: There is a major plot twist halfway through that changes how you see the characters.
vocabulary.exampleAR: هناك التواء كبير في الحبكة في منتصف الفيلم يغير نظرتك للشخصيات.

vocabulary.definition: How a character changes or grows during a story.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Good character development helps the audience care about what happens next.
vocabulary.exampleAR: تطوّر الشخصيات الجيد يساعد الجمهور على الاهتمام بما سيحدث لاحقاً.

vocabulary.definition: Visual or sound techniques used in film to create scenes that are hard to film in reality.
vocabulary.exampleEN: The special effects were impressive but sometimes distracted from the story.
vocabulary.exampleAR: كانت المؤثرات الخاصة مثيرة للإعجاب لكنها أحياناً شغلت عن القصة.

vocabulary.definition: A book that is so exciting or interesting that the reader keeps turning pages.
vocabulary.exampleEN: The mystery novel is an absolute page-turner; I finished it in two evenings.
vocabulary.exampleAR: رواية الغموض هذه لا تُصبح مليئة بالطاقة؛ أنهيتها في ليلتين.

vocabulary.definition: Causing you to think seriously about ideas or issues.
vocabulary.exampleEN: The film is thought-provoking and raises questions about identity.
vocabulary.exampleAR: الفيلم يثير التفكير ويطرح أسئلة عن الهوية.

vocabulary.definition: Suitable for viewers of different ages, including children.
vocabulary.exampleEN: The new animated film is family-friendly and has jokes adults will enjoy too.
vocabulary.exampleAR: الفيلم الرسومي الجديد مناسب للعائلة ويحتوي على نكات تستمتع بها البالغون أيضاً.

vocabulary.definition: A storyline that keeps the audience interested.
vocabulary.exampleEN: An engaging plot and strong dialogue kept the audience involved from start to finish.
vocabulary.exampleAR: حبكة جذابة وحوار قوي أبقيا الجمهور مشدوداً من البداية إلى النهاية.

grammar.topic: Evaluative adjectives and recommendation language
grammar.concept: Use precise evaluative adjectives (e.g. compelling, predictable, underwhelming) to state opinions and combine them with recommendation structures (I would recommend, It's worth) and qualifiers (probably, slightly) to show degree.
grammar.arabicComparison: الصفات التقييمية تُعطي رأياً مباشراً، بينما عبارات التوصية تخبر القارئ ماذا يفعل. استخدم مؤشرات الدرجة (مثل slightly, really) لتليين أو تقوية الرأي.
grammar.structure: Basic patterns: 1) It was + evaluative adjective (+ because + reason). 2) I would (strongly/highly/probably) recommend + noun/gerund + to + audience. 3) If you like + genre/aspect, you'll + verb.
grammar.commonError: Overusing very + adjective (very good) without detail; or giving a recommendation without saying who will like it.
grammar.exampleEN: It was underwhelming because the plot was predictable. I would probably recommend it to fans of the lead actor, but not to viewers who want original stories.
grammar.exampleAR: كان مخيباً لأن الحبكة كانت متوقعة. ربما أنصح به لمحبي الممثل الرئيسي، لكن ليس للمشاهدين الذين يريدون قصصاً أصلية.

readingBrief: Read an original 250–350-word review article of a recent film. The review will present a short summary, highlight two strengths and one weakness with concrete examples (an actor's performance, a plot twist, or the use of effects), mention who will enjoy the film, and finish with a clear recommendation. The piece models balanced language, evaluative adjectives, and recommendation phrases you can use in your own writing.
writingPrompt: Write a short review (140–180 words) for the student magazine about a recent book, film or cultural experience. Audience: classmates and other students. Purpose: give your opinion, support it with two specific examples, and end with a clear recommendation. Success criteria: organise your review into a brief introduction, two short supporting paragraphs (summary plus evaluation), and a one-sentence conclusion with recommendation; use at least two evaluative adjectives and at least one recommendation phrase (e.g. I would recommend, worth seeing). Maintain a balanced, semi-formal tone suitable for fellow students.

title: Learning how to learn

outcome.canDo: I can describe my learning progress, explain strategies I have tried, and ask for constructive feedback using the present perfect simple and continuous.
outcome.canDoArabic: أستطيع وصف تقدمي في التعلم وشرح الاستراتيجيات التي جرّبتها وطلب ملاحظات بنّاءة باستخدام المضارع التام البسيط والمستمر.
outcome.scenario: You have been studying for a professional course for several months. You need to write an update to your tutor explaining what you have been doing, what progress you have made, and what help you need next.
outcome.scenarioArabic: أنت تدرس دورة مهنية منذ عدة أشهر. عليك كتابة تقرير موجز إلى مدرسك تشرح فيه ما الذي كنت تفعله، وما التقدّم الذي أحرزته، وما المساعدة التي تحتاجها لاحقًا.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Think of one time when you changed how you studied (an experience). Write 4–6 short sentences describing: what you used to do, what you changed, and why you changed it. Include one sentence about whether the change helped (opinion).
retrieval.purpose: Repurpose A2 experience/opinion language into a linked short narrative that prepares learners to report progress at B1 level.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Make a simple plan (4 points) for the next four weeks of your learning. Include one new strategy you will try and one service or support you will use (e.g. tutor session, app).
retrieval.purpose: Convert A2 plans/services language into a specific, measurable plan that will be described in B1 writing.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Say briefly which study activities you prefer and why (2–3 sentences). Then add one change you would like to make to your routine.
retrieval.purpose: Reuse A2 preferences/change language to prompt reflection that feeds B1-level descriptive language.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: List two opinions about feedback (positive or negative) and give a short reason for each. Example: 'I think feedback is useful because…'.
retrieval.purpose: Move simple opinion language toward reasoned comments that will appear in a connected update or email.

priorLevelLinks: Module 4 Lesson 12: Daily habits for learning
Module 4 Lesson 14: Making plans and choices
network.learningNote: Focus on connecting short actions (set goals, try a strategy) with results (I have improved, I have been practising). The present perfect simple describes completed changes; the present perfect continuous emphasises ongoing activity.
network.learningNoteArabic: ركّز على ربط الإجراءات القصيرة (وضع أهداف، تجربة استراتيجية) مع النتائج (لقد تحسّنت، كنت أتدرّب). المضارع التام البسيط يصف تغيّرات مكتملة؛ المضارع التام المستمر يركّز على نشاط مستمر.

wordFamilies.note: Use 'learning' for activities and 'learner' for a person.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: استخدم 'learning' للأنشطة و'learner' للشخص.

wordFamilies.note: Reflection is the process; reflective describes a person or comment.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: الـ reflection هي العملية؛ reflective يصف الشخص أو التعليق.

wordFamilies.note: As a verb, 'to progress' is less common in daily learning talk than 'make progress'.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: كفعل 'to progress' أقل شيوعًا للمحادثات اليومية عن التعلم من 'make progress'.

vocabulary.definition: Decide specific targets you want to achieve in your learning.
vocabulary.exampleEN: At the start of each week I set goals for vocabulary and speaking practice.
vocabulary.exampleAR: في بداية كل أسبوع أعيّن أهدافًا لحفظ المفردات وممارسة المحادثة.

vocabulary.definition: Monitor how much you are improving over time.
vocabulary.exampleEN: I track progress by keeping a short log of what I studied each day.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أتتبع التقدّم بتسجيل قصير لما درسته كل يوم.

vocabulary.definition: Request comments from others to understand strengths and areas to improve.
vocabulary.exampleEN: After the presentation, I asked for feedback from my tutor and classmates.
vocabulary.exampleAR: بعد العرض التقديمي طلبت ملاحظات من مدرسّي وزملائي.

vocabulary.definition: A personal review of your performance or skills.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Do a brief self-assessment once a month to see what is working.
vocabulary.exampleAR: قم بتقييم ذاتي موجز مرة في الشهر لمعرفة ما ينجح.

vocabulary.definition: A planned method for improving learning (e.g. spaced practice, flashcards).
vocabulary.exampleEN: His learning strategy includes short daily reviews and weekly tests.
vocabulary.exampleAR: تتضمن استراتيجية تعلّمه مراجعات يومية قصيرة واختبارات أسبوعية.

vocabulary.definition: Think carefully about an experience or your performance.
vocabulary.exampleEN: I reflected on my exam and realised I needed more speaking practice.
vocabulary.exampleAR: تأملت في امتحاني وأدركت أنني بحاجة لممارسة تحدث أكثر.

vocabulary.definition: Improve gradually and continuously over time.
vocabulary.exampleEN: She has been making steady progress with her pronunciation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: لقد كانت تُحرز تقدّمًا ثابتًا في النطق.

vocabulary.definition: A repeated cycle of receiving feedback and making improvements.
vocabulary.exampleEN: A quick feedback loop helped him correct mistakes before the exam.
vocabulary.exampleAR: ساعدته حلقة ملاحظات سريعة على تصحيح الأخطاء قبل الامتحان.

vocabulary.definition: Accept responsibility for your own learning and decisions.
vocabulary.exampleEN: If you take ownership of your study plan, you are more likely to succeed.
vocabulary.exampleAR: إذا تحمّلت مسؤولية خطة دراستك، فستكون أكثر عرضة للنجاح.

vocabulary.definition: Decide which tasks are most important and do them first.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Prioritise difficult tasks when you are most focused.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أعطِ الأولوية للمهام الصعبة عندما تكون أكثر تركيزًا.

vocabulary.definition: Keep going with an activity despite difficulties.
vocabulary.exampleEN: She persisted with listening practice even though progress was slow.
vocabulary.exampleAR: استمرت في ممارسة الاستماع رغم أن التقدّم كان بطيئًا.

vocabulary.definition: A way of dealing with a learning task or problem.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Try a different approach if your current method hasn't been helping.
vocabulary.exampleAR: جرّب نهجًا مختلفًا إذا لم تكن طريقتك الحالية مفيدة.

grammar.topic: Present perfect simple and present perfect continuous
grammar.arabicName: المضارع التام البسيط والمضارع التام المستمر
grammar.concept: Use the present perfect simple (have/has + past participle) for completed actions or results with present relevance; use the present perfect continuous (have/has been + -ing) for actions that started in the past and are still happening or were happening recently.
grammar.arabicComparison: يُستخدم المضارع التام البسيط (have/has + التصريف الثالث) للأفعال المكتملة أو النتائج ذات صلة بالحاضر؛ ويُستخدم المضارع التام المستمر (have/has been + فعل-ing) للأفعال التي بدأت في الماضي وما زالت مستمرة أو حدثت مؤخرًا وكانت مستمرة.
grammar.structure: Simple: subject + have/has + past participle. Continuous: subject + have/has been + verb-ing.
grammar.commonError: Learners often use the present perfect continuous with finished actions (e.g. 'I have been finished') or forget 'been' in the continuous form.
grammar.exampleEN: Simple: I have improved my vocabulary this month. Continuous: I have been practising pronunciation every day this week.
grammar.exampleAR: بسيط: لقد طوّرت مفرداتي هذا الشهر. مستمر: لقد كنت أتمرّن على النطق كل يوم هذا الأسبوع.

readingBrief: Write an original 250–350-word interview between a course tutor and a learner. The learner explains what they have been doing for the past three months, which strategies they have tried, and what progress they have made. The tutor asks questions and gives short, constructive feedback and suggestions. The interview should show examples of present perfect simple and continuous in realistic, connected turns and end with a plan for the next steps.
writingPrompt: Write a 140–180-word email to your course tutor. Audience: your tutor. Purpose: explain what you have been doing lately, summarise the progress you have made, and ask for two specific pieces of feedback or help. Success criteria: use the present perfect simple and continuous correctly; organise the email with a short opening, two clear paragraphs (activities/strategies and progress/request for help), and a polite closing; keep a polite and reflective tone.

title: A career conversation

outcome.canDo: I can explain my career goals, describe relevant qualifications and experience, and speculate about possible next steps in my career.
outcome.canDoArabic: أستطيع أن أشرح أهدافي المهنية، وأصف المؤهلات والخبرات المناسبة، وأتحدث عن الاحتمالات المحتملة لمساري المهني.
outcome.scenario: You meet an HR advisor and a former colleague to discuss your next career move. You explain your skills and qualifications, respond to questions in an interview-style conversation, and suggest possible steps you might take next.
outcome.scenarioArabic: تلتقى بمستشار موارد بشرية وزميل سابق لمناقشة خطوتك المهنية التالية. تشرح مهاراتك ومؤهلاتك، وتجيب عن أسئلة على طراز مقابلة، وتقترح خطوات محتملة قد تتخذها لاحقًا.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: List three past experiences (jobs, volunteering, courses) and one skill you used in each. Then note one thing you preferred or disliked about each role.
retrieval.purpose: Repurposes A2 experience and preferences into material you will use to give a connected B1 account of your qualifications.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Say what you plan to do next year (course, job search, move, change of hours) and why. Include one reason you might change that plan.
retrieval.purpose: Uses A2 plans and change to prepare speculative sentences (may/might/could) for a B1 discussion of future steps.

retrieval.language: Arabic
retrieval.prompt: اكتب عن خدمة أو تدريب تقدمت له أو استخدمته (خدمة وظائف، دورة تدريبية). صف رأيك فيها ولماذا قد تنصح أو لا تنصح بها.
retrieval.purpose: يسترجع لغة A2 عن الخدمات والآراء ويجهز معلومات عملية لحديث مهنى أكثر تطورا (B1).

network.learningNote: Teach vocabulary as useful chunks and collocations. Emphasise using may/might/could to speculate about likely career steps and use organised paragraphs when giving opinions or making requests.
network.learningNoteArabic: علّم المفردات على شكل عبارات وأزواج كلمات مفيدة. ركز على استخدام may/might/could للتكهن بالخطوات المهنية المستقبلية واستخدم فقرات منظمة عند إبداء الرأي أو طلب مساعدة.

wordFamilies.note: Verbs and nouns used to talk about certificates and meeting requirements.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: أفعال وأسماء متعلقة بالشهادات وتلبية المتطلبات.

wordFamilies.note: Verbs and nouns for sending CVs, forms and being a candidate.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: أفعال وأسماء لإرسال السيرة الذاتية والنماذج والتقدم للوظائف.

wordFamilies.note: Useful for talking about supervising others and moving into leadership roles.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: مفيدة للحديث عن الإشراف والانتقال إلى أدوار قيادية.

vocabulary.definition: The process of improving skills and advancing in one's job over time.
vocabulary.exampleEN: She sees training as part of her career development and might change jobs next year.
vocabulary.exampleAR: ترى أن التدريب جزء من تطورها المهني وقد تغيّر وظيفتها العام المقبل.

vocabulary.definition: A formal meeting in which an employer asks about a candidate's suitability for a role.
vocabulary.exampleEN: I have a job interview next Tuesday for the assistant role.
vocabulary.exampleAR: لدي مقابلة عمل يوم الثلاثاء المقبل لدور مساعد.
