vocabulary.definition: To accept tasks or duties that someone is accountable for.
vocabulary.exampleEN: After the promotion she began to take on responsibility for the small team.
vocabulary.exampleAR: بعد الترقية بدأت تتحمل مسؤولية الفريق الصغير.

vocabulary.definition: To change jobs or roles in order to start supervising people or projects.
vocabulary.exampleEN: He hopes to move into management within two years.
vocabulary.exampleAR: يرجو الانتقال إلى الإدارة خلال سنتين.

vocabulary.definition: Being one of the final candidates considered for a job or opportunity.
vocabulary.exampleEN: She was on a shortlist for the training programme.
vocabulary.exampleAR: كانت في القائمة النهائية لبرنامج التدريب.

vocabulary.definition: Abilities for communicating and working well with others.
vocabulary.exampleEN: His strong interpersonal skills could make him a good team leader.
vocabulary.exampleAR: قد تجعل مهاراته الشخصية القوية منه قائد فريق جيد.

vocabulary.definition: To formally request to be considered for a job, course, or service.
vocabulary.exampleEN: She will apply for the scholarship next month.
vocabulary.exampleAR: سوف تتقدم للمنحة الشهر القادم.

vocabulary.definition: To contact someone, often to ask for information or arrange a meeting.
vocabulary.exampleEN: I'll get in touch with the recruiter tomorrow to ask about the interview date.
vocabulary.exampleAR: سأتواصل مع مسؤول التوظيف غداً للسؤال عن موعد المقابلة.

vocabulary.definition: A period when someone stops working to do something else, like travel or care for family.
vocabulary.exampleEN: She took a career break to care for her children and is now ready to return.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أخذت فترة توقف عن العمل لرعاية أطفالها وهي الآن جاهزة للعودة.

vocabulary.definition: To have the required qualifications or skills for a role.
vocabulary.exampleEN: If you meet the criteria, you may be selected for the next round.
vocabulary.exampleAR: إذا استوفيت الشروط، فقد يتم اختيارك للجولة التالية.

vocabulary.definition: A certificate or skill that shows a person is able to do a particular job.
vocabulary.exampleEN: A teaching qualification is required for that position.
vocabulary.exampleAR: مطلوب مؤهل تدريسي لهذا المنصب.

vocabulary.definition: Having a strong desire to succeed or achieve a high position.
vocabulary.exampleEN: He's ambitious and hopes he might manage a department one day.
vocabulary.exampleAR: هو طموح ويأمل أن يدير قسمًا يومًا ما.

grammar.topic: speculation about present and future
grammar.concept: Use modal verbs (may, might, could) and structures such as be likely to / could be + -ing to guess about what is happening now or what may happen later. Use present continuous for planned near future and may/might/could for uncertainty.
grammar.arabicComparison: نستخدم may/might/could للتكهن بالمستقبل أو الحاضر غير المؤكد، وbe + -ing للخطط المؤكدة بالقرب، بينما تُستخدم will للتنبؤات الأقوى.
grammar.structure: may/might/could + base verb; be + likely/unlikely + to + verb; could be + -ing; present continuous for planned future (I am meeting...).
grammar.commonError: Using 'will' for uncertain present situations (e.g. 'He will be at home' instead of 'He might be at home') or mixing present continuous with may incorrectly.
grammar.exampleEN: She may be working in London now. He might move into management next year. I'm meeting the HR advisor on Friday, so I could be offered a new role soon.
grammar.exampleAR: قد تكون تعمل في لندن الآن. قد ينتقل إلى الإدارة العام المقبل. سألتقي مستشار الموارد البشرية يوم الجمعة، لذلك قد يُعرض عليه دور جديد قريبًا.

readingBrief: Read an original 250–350-word interview with a mid-level professional who changed their career after a short career break. The piece should include: a brief personal background, reasons for the break, the steps they took to retrain or gain qualifications, at least two examples of transferable skills, and reflections on what they might do next (speculation using may/might/could). Use this article to identify language for describing experience, qualifications and speculative sentences about future plans.
writingPrompt: Write a professional email (140–180 words) to a career advisor at a training centre. Audience: career advisor. Purpose: explain your recent work experience and qualifications, state your career goal, and ask for advice on next steps or relevant courses. Success criteria: organise your email into clear paragraphs (one for background, one for current goal, one for request), use a professional tone, and include at least two speculative sentences using may/might/could to describe possible next steps.

title: Travel when plans change

outcome.canDo: I can explain what happened when travel plans changed, politely negotiate a fair solution, and describe earlier events using the past perfect.
outcome.canDoArabic: أستطيع شرح ما حدث عندما تغيّرت الخطط، والتفاوض بأدب للحصول على حل عادل، ووصف الأحداث السابقة باستخدام الماضي التام.
outcome.scenario: You arrive at the airport to find your flight overbooked and your itinerary changed. You must tell customer service what happened, state what you had already done, and politely negotiate an alternative or compensation.
outcome.scenarioArabic: تصل إلى المطار فتكتشف أن الرحلة مُزدحمة وأن خط سير رحلتك تغير. عليك إخبار خدمة العملاء بما حدث، وبيان ما كنت قد فعلته سابقًا، والتفاوض بأدب للحصول على بديل أو تعويض.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Describe a past travel experience (what happened) and say what you had already done before the problem (use past simple + past perfect).
retrieval.purpose: Repurpose A2 'experiences' and 'change' language to practise past perfect and sequencing for a B1 narrative.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Explain your usual travel plans and preferences, then describe a time when those plans changed and how you reacted.
retrieval.purpose: Use A2 'plans' and 'preferences' to build a connected B1 account requiring cause, effect and negotiation language.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Think of a time you used a service (hotel, airline, transport). Say what went wrong and whether you asked for help or a refund.
retrieval.purpose: Repurpose A2 'services' and 'opinions' into a B1 problem-solution narrative that includes making a request.

retrieval.language: Arabic
retrieval.prompt: اخبر عن مرّة تغيّرت فيها خطط سفرك فجأة. ماذا شعرت وفعلت؟ (استخدم الماضي البسيط والماضي التام إذا أمكن).
retrieval.purpose: تحويل مفردات A2 عن 'التجارب' و'التغيير' إلى مهمة B1 تركز على تسلسل الأحداث والتفاوض.

network.anchor: When plans change, how do you get a fair outcome?
network.learningNote: Focus on connecting events (use past perfect) and on polite language for negotiation (modals and hedging). Practise set phrases for customer service situations.
network.learningNoteArabic: ركّز على ربط الأحداث (الماضي التام) وعلى لغة التفاوض المهذبة (الأفعال المساعدة والأساليب المخففة). درّب عبارات جاهزة لمواقف خدمة العملاء.

wordFamilies.note: Used for events and policy changes; can be noun or verb.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: تُستخدم للأحداث وتغيّر السياسات؛ يمكن أن تكون اسمًا أو فعلًا.

wordFamilies.note: Often used with compensation and formal requests.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: تستخدم غالبًا مع التعويض والطلبات الرسمية.

wordFamilies.note: Useful for making practical solutions; noun form 'arrangement' is common.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: مفيدة لاقتراح حلول عملية؛ صيغة الاسم 'arrangement' شائعة.

vocabulary.definition: A situation where what was planned no longer happens and must be altered.
vocabulary.exampleEN: A sudden storm meant a change of plans for our flight schedule.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أدت العاصفة المفاجئة إلى تغيير في الخطط لجدول رحلاتنا.

vocabulary.definition: To fail to catch a connecting flight or transport because of a delay or timing.
vocabulary.exampleEN: We missed a connection after our first flight was delayed.
vocabulary.exampleAR: فقدنا رحلة التوصيل بعد أن تأخرت رحلتنا الأولى.

vocabulary.definition: A policy that covers certain losses or costs during travel, like delays or cancellations.
vocabulary.exampleEN: I bought travel insurance in case I needed to cancel or change the trip.
vocabulary.exampleAR: اشتريت تأمين السفر تحسبًا للحاجة لإلغاء أو تغيير الرحلة.

vocabulary.definition: Politely ask an airline or provider to issue a voucher to cover future travel when a booking is disrupted.
vocabulary.exampleEN: By the time the desk reopened, I had already requested a travel voucher for the cancelled flight.
vocabulary.exampleAR: بحلول الوقت الذي أعيد فيه افتتاح المكتب، كنت قد طلبت بالفعل قسيمة سفر عن الرحلة الملغاة.

vocabulary.definition: A formal request for money or another remedy because of loss or inconvenience.
vocabulary.exampleEN: They submitted a compensation claim for the missed business meeting.
vocabulary.exampleAR: قدّموا مطالبة بالتعويض عن فقدان اجتماع العمل.

vocabulary.definition: A ticket that allows travel if there is space available, often without a guaranteed seat.
vocabulary.exampleEN: He took a stand-by ticket hoping to get on an earlier flight.
vocabulary.exampleAR: حصل على تذكرة انتظار على أمل ركوب رحلة مبكرة.

vocabulary.definition: The document or card that allows a passenger to board a plane.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Keep your boarding pass until you have collected your luggage.
vocabulary.exampleAR: احتفظ ببطاقة الصعود حتى تجمع أمتعتك.

vocabulary.definition: A flight with more passengers booked than available seats.
vocabulary.exampleEN: An overbooked flight left several passengers without seats.
vocabulary.exampleAR: تركت الرحلة المحجوزة زيادة عدة ركاب بدون مقاعد.

vocabulary.definition: A modification to the planned route, times or stops of a trip.
vocabulary.exampleEN: The airline sent a message about an itinerary change due to maintenance.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أرسلت شركة الطيران رسالة بشأن تغيير في خط سير الرحلة بسبب أعمال صيانة.

vocabulary.definition: Legal or policy protections passengers have in cases like delays or cancellations.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Learn your passenger rights before you travel so you know what to ask for.
vocabulary.exampleAR: تعرف على حقوق الركاب قبل السفر لتعرف ما الذي يمكنك المطالبة به.

vocabulary.definition: To say or do something to remove someone's doubts or fears.
vocabulary.exampleEN: The agent tried to reassure us that an alternative would be found.
vocabulary.exampleAR: حاول الموظف أن يطمئننا بأنه سيتم إيجاد بديل.

vocabulary.definition: A different plan or solution offered to replace the original one.
vocabulary.exampleEN: They offered an alternative arrangement: a later flight with a hotel voucher.
vocabulary.exampleAR: عرضوا ترتيبًا بديلاً: رحلة لاحقة وقسيمة فندق.

grammar.topic: Polite negotiation and past perfect
grammar.concept: Use past perfect to show that one past action happened before another (e.g. 'I had checked in before they cancelled the flight'). Use polite negotiation language (modals, hedges and set phrases) to request solutions without sounding rude.
grammar.arabicComparison: يُستخدم الماضي التام للإشارة إلى حدث سبق حدثًا آخر في الماضي؛ في العربية نستخدم غالبًا الماضي مع كلمات مثل 'قبل' للتعبير عن ذلك. وللتفاوض المهذب نستخدم أساليب مخففة مثل 'هل من الممكن' أو صيغ الشرط.
grammar.structure: Past perfect: had + past participle. Polite negotiation: modal + subject + verb (Could we possibly receive a refund? Would you mind checking?), hedges like 'perhaps', 'maybe', and set phrases: 'I was wondering if...' 'Would it be possible to...'.
grammar.commonError: Using past simple where past perfect is needed (e.g. 'I checked in before they cancelled' without showing sequence) and making direct demands instead of polite requests.
grammar.exampleEN: I had already checked in when the airline informed me the flight was overbooked, so I asked if they could offer an alternative arrangement.
grammar.exampleAR: كنت قد سجّلت الوصول بالفعل عندما أخبرتني شركة الطيران أن الرحلة مزدحمة زيادة، فطلبت منهم إن كانوا يستطيعون تقديم ترتيب بديل.

readingBrief: Read an original 250–350-word email from a passenger to an airline. The message describes how the passenger's plans changed (delays, missed connections, itinerary change), explains what they had already done (use past perfect), and politely asks for an alternative arrangement or compensation. While reading, identify past perfect uses and three polite negotiation phrases.
writingPrompt: Write a 140–180 word formal email to an airline customer service agent. Purpose: explain the problem (what happened and what you had already done), state the impact on your plans, and politely request a specific solution (alternative arrangement or compensation). Audience: airline customer service. Success criterion: organise your email into three clear paragraphs (1: situation, 2: actions you had taken, 3: request and proposed solution) and keep a polite, professional tone throughout.

title: Small choices, wider effects

outcome.canDo: I can describe small everyday choices and explain their possible wider effects using conditionals and consequence clauses.
outcome.canDoArabic: أستطيع وصف الخيارات اليومية الصغيرة وشرح آثارها الأوسع المحتملة باستخدام الجمل الشرطية وجمل العواقب.
outcome.scenario: You are writing a short proposal to your local community group explaining how a few small changes (e.g. reducing single-use plastic, choosing seasonal food, using a repair service) could lead to broader benefits for the neighbourhood. You must mention trade-offs and possible consequences.
outcome.scenarioArabic: أنت تكتب اقتراحًا قصيرًا لمجموعة المجتمع المحلي تشرح فيه كيف أن بعض التغييرات الصغيرة (مثل تقليل البلاستيك ذو الاستخدام الواحد، اختيار الطعام الموسمي، استخدام خدمات الإصلاح) يمكن أن تؤدي إلى فوائد أوسع للحي. يجب أن تذكر المفاضلات والعواقب المحتملة.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Think of one small change you already made (experience) and one change you plan to try (plan). Say which you prefer and why, then explain what would happen if everyone in your building made the same small change (use a conditional).
retrieval.purpose: Repurpose A2 language (experiences, plans, preferences) into a connected B1 response that includes a conditional result and a short explanation of consequences.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Compare two local services (e.g. municipal recycling vs. a private collection service). Describe their benefits and downsides (opinions, services, change) and weigh up the trade-offs using conditional language (if… then… / unless…).
retrieval.purpose: Reuse A2 vocabulary about services and opinions to produce a balanced B1-level evaluation with conditional clauses expressing likely outcomes.

retrieval.language: Arabic
retrieval.prompt: اذكر تفضيلًا بين خيارين لخفض النفايات (تجربة أو خطة). صف رأيك وأي تغيير ستقترحه، ثم اشرح نتيجة محتملة إذا تبنّى الجميع هذا التغيير (استخدم جملة شرطية).
retrieval.purpose: إعادة استخدام مفردات A2 حول التفضيلات والتغيير في مهمة B1 تطلب سردًا مترابطًا مع عبارات شرطية لعواقب محتملة.

priorLevelLinks: A2 Speaking: Talking about plans and preferences
network.learningNote: At B1 we use conditionals to link small actions to wider consequences. Focus on first and second conditionals (real and hypothetical) and linking phrases (so, therefore, as a result) to make cause–effect clear.
network.learningNoteArabic: في مستوى B1 نستخدم الجمل الشرطية لربط الإجراءات الصغيرة بالعواقب الأوسع. ركّز على الشرط الأول والثاني والروابط (so, therefore, as a result) لتوضيح العلاقة سبب-نتيجة.

wordFamilies.note: Use different forms to talk about habits (consume less), statistics (consumption), or people (consumer).
wordFamilies.noteArabic: استخدم الأشكال المختلفة للحديث عن العادات (consume less)، أو الإحصاءات (consumption)، أو الأشخاص (consumer).

wordFamilies.note: Pair with objects (reduce waste, reduction in costs) and with modal verbs (can reduce).
wordFamilies.noteArabic: اجمعها مع مفعولات (reduce waste، reduction in costs) ومع أفعال مساعدة (can reduce).

wordFamilies.note: sustainable and sustainability are common adjectives/nouns for environmental topics.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: sustainable و sustainability شائعة كصفة واسم في مواضيع البيئة.

vocabulary.definition: Minor everyday decisions that collectively influence outcomes.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Wearing a jumper instead of turning up the heating is one of the small choices that can reduce energy use.
vocabulary.exampleAR: ارتداء سترة بدلاً من رفع التدفئة هو أحد الخيارات الصغيرة التي يمكن أن تقلل استخدام الطاقة.

vocabulary.definition: Broader consequences that follow from a set of actions or decisions.
vocabulary.exampleEN: If the whole street starts composting, the wider effects could include less rubbish and richer soil in community gardens.
vocabulary.exampleAR: إذا بدأ الشارع كله في تسميد النفايات، فقد تشمل الآثار الأوسع تقليلاً للنفايات وتربة أغنى في حدائق المجتمع.

vocabulary.definition: A situation in which choosing one thing involves losing or giving up another.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Choosing organic food can be healthier, but there is often a trade-off in higher price or limited availability.
vocabulary.exampleAR: اختيار الطعام العضوي يمكن أن يكون أكثر صحة، لكن غالبًا ما يكون هناك مقايضة في ارتفاع السعر أو محدودية التوفر.

vocabulary.definition: To consider the advantages and disadvantages before deciding.
vocabulary.exampleEN: We should weigh up the environmental benefits against the extra cost before changing the service.
vocabulary.exampleAR: يجب أن نوازن بين الفوائد البيئية والتكلفة الإضافية قبل تغيير الخدمة.

vocabulary.definition: To have a negative consequence or require payment of resources, time, or money.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Installing solar panels can save money long-term but may come at a cost at the start.
vocabulary.exampleAR: تركيب الألواح الشمسية يمكن أن يوفر المال على المدى الطويل لكنه قد يأتي بتكلفة في البداية.

vocabulary.definition: The total greenhouse gas emissions caused directly and indirectly by a person or organisation.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Flying increases your carbon footprint more than taking the train.
vocabulary.exampleAR: السفر بالطائرة يزيد بصمة الكربون لديك أكثر من السفر بالقطار.

vocabulary.definition: To cut down on the amount of rubbish produced.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Many cafés now offer discounts if you bring a reusable cup to help reduce waste.
vocabulary.exampleAR: العديد من المقاهي الآن تقدم خصومات إذا أحضرت كوبًا قابلاً لإعادة الاستخدام للمساعدة في تقليل النفايات.

vocabulary.definition: A choice that meets present needs without harming future resources or environments.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Using local suppliers is often a more sustainable option than ordering internationally.
vocabulary.exampleAR: استخدام الموردين المحليين غالبًا ما يكون خيارًا أكثر استدامة من الطلب من الخارج.

vocabulary.definition: To cause something to become different, especially improvements over time
vocabulary.exampleEN: If enough people recycle, it can bring about change in how companies package their products.
vocabulary.exampleAR: إذا قام عدد كافٍ من الناس بإعادة التدوير، فقد يُؤدّي ذلك إلى تغيّر في طريقة تعبئة الشركات لمنتجاتها.

vocabulary.definition: To use fewer goods, energy, or resources.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Families who consume less electricity often save money and reduce their carbon footprint.
vocabulary.exampleAR: الأسر التي تستهلك كهرباء أقل غالبًا ما توفر المال وتقلل بصمة الكربون الخاصة بها.

vocabulary.definition: A shift in habits or routines that affects how people act over time.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Behaviour change campaigns aim to make recycling an easy and normal habit.
vocabulary.exampleAR: تهدف حملات تغيير السلوك إلى جعل إعادة التدوير عادة سهلة وطبيعية.

vocabulary.definition: An effect that becomes clear only after a long period of time.
vocabulary.exampleEN: One long-term consequence of overfishing is the collapse of local fish stocks.
vocabulary.exampleAR: إحدى العواقب بعيدة المدى للصيد الجائر هي انهيار مخزونات الأسماك المحلية.

grammar.topic: Conditionals and consequence clauses
grammar.concept: Use first and second conditionals to link actions and their possible results, and use consequence clauses (so / therefore / as a result) to show cause and effect.
grammar.arabicComparison: استخدم الشرط الأول للحالات الواقعية المحتملة (If + present, will + verb) والشرط الثاني للخيالات أو الاحتمالات المنخفضة (If + past, would + verb). استخدم so/therefore/as a result لربط السبب بالنتيجة.
grammar.structure: First conditional: If + present simple, will + base verb. Second conditional: If + past simple, would + base verb. Consequence clauses: main clause + so / therefore / as a result + result clause.
grammar.commonError: Putting 'will' in the if-clause (e.g. *If we will recycle, we will save money). Also mixing tenses incorrectly between condition and result.
grammar.exampleEN: If we reduce packaging, we will create less rubbish, so the streets will be cleaner. If we had a local repair café, people would fix more items, and this would reduce consumption.
grammar.exampleAR: إذا قمنا بتقليل التغليف فسننتج نفايات أقل، لذلك ستكون الشوارع أنظف. لو كان لدينا مقهى إصلاح محلي، لكان الناس يصلحون المزيد من الأشياء، وهذا سيقلل من الاستهلاك.

readingBrief: Read an original 250–350-word interview with a community organiser who started a low-cost repair café. The interview explains why they began (a small local choice), the trade-offs they faced (time, funding, volunteers), and the wider effects over two years (reduced waste, new skills, stronger neighbourhood ties). The article includes at least two conditionals predicting future outcomes if the project expands.
writingPrompt: Write a 140–180-word formal proposal (email or short letter) to your local councillor explaining one small action your street could adopt and the likely wider effects. Audience: local councillor; Purpose: convince them to support a pilot initiative. Success criteria: organise your text into three clear paragraphs (1: introduce the action and why you suggest it; 2: explain benefits and trade-offs using at least one conditional; 3: conclude with a polite request), and maintain a polite, formal tone throughout.

title: A question worth debating

outcome.canDo: I can present a structured argument on a local issue, use evidence and a clear concession to respond to a counterargument, and write a short balanced opinion.
outcome.canDoArabic: يمكنني عرض حجة منظمة حول قضية محلية، استخدام الأدلة وتقديم تنازل واضح للرد على حجة مضادة، وكتابة رأي قصير ومتوازن.
outcome.scenario: Your town council proposes a new traffic scheme for the high street. You need to write to the council and speak at a community meeting to explain your position, support it with evidence, acknowledge one reasonable objection, and recommend a practical solution.
outcome.scenarioArabic: اقترح مجلس البلدة خطة جديدة لحركة المرور في الشارع الرئيسي. تحتاج إلى كتابة رسالة إلى المجلس والتحدث في اجتماع المجتمع لشرح موقفك، دعمه بالأدلة، الاعتراف باعتراض واحد معقول، واقتراح حل عملي.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Think of a recent experience in your area (e.g., a change in a shop, a new bus route, or a road closure). Briefly describe what happened and how it affected you (2–3 sentences).
retrieval.purpose: Activate an A2-level personal experience to provide concrete examples you can use as evidence in a B1 argument.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Describe any plans you know about local services (e.g., opening times, bus schedules, recycling changes). Say whether you support those plans and why (2–3 sentences).
retrieval.purpose: Use A2 knowledge of plans to practice giving reasons and evidence for an opinion.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Say one preference you have about a local service (e.g., I prefer buses that run later). Give one short reason for that preference.
retrieval.purpose: Turn a simple preference into the start of an argument (preference + reason).

retrieval.language: Arabic
retrieval.prompt: اذكر خدمة محلية تتأثر بالتغيير (مثل مواقف السيارات أو الحافلات). كيف يؤثر التغيير على الناس في منطقتك؟ (جملة أو جملتان)
retrieval.purpose: تذكُّر معلومات عملية عن الخدمات يساعدك في تقديم أمثلة واقعية كدليل في حجتك.

network.learningNote: Teach chunks as functional tools: students should be able to link a claim to supporting evidence, offer a short concession, and respond to a counterargument. Model organisation: introduction (position), reasons with evidence, acknowledge one objection (concession), reply, recommendation.
network.learningNoteArabic: علّم العبارات كأدوات وظيفية: يجب أن يتمكن الطلاب من ربط الادعاء بالأدلة، تقديم تنازل قصير، والرد على حجة مضادة. نمذَج التنظيم: مقدمة (الموقف)، أسباب مع أدلة، الاعتراف باعتراض واحد (تنازل)، رد، توصية.

wordFamilies.note: Use 'argument' for a reasoned set of points; 'argue' is the action; 'argumentative' describes a style.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: استخدم 'argument' للأفكار المنظمة؛ 'argue' للفعل؛ 'argumentative' لوصف أسلوب.

wordFamilies.note: Focus on sources and quality: strong/weak evidence, reliable sources.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: ركز على المصادر والجودة: دليل قوي/ضعيف، مصادر موثوقة.

wordFamilies.note: Use convincing arguments and evidence to persuade rather than strong language alone.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: استخدم حججًا وأدلة مقنعة للإقناع بدلاً من اللغة القوية فقط.

vocabulary.definition: to give reasons and evidence to support an opinion or proposal
vocabulary.exampleEN: She made a strong case for more bike lanes, citing safety statistics.
vocabulary.exampleAR: قدمت حجة قوية من أجل المزيد من ممرات الدراجات، مستشهدة بإحصاءات السلامة.

vocabulary.definition: to show facts, data or documents that support a claim
vocabulary.exampleEN: At the meeting, residents presented evidence of increased traffic at school time.
vocabulary.exampleAR: في الاجتماع قدم السكان أدلة على زيادة حركة المرور في وقت المدرسة.

vocabulary.definition: an argument that disagrees with or opposes another argument
vocabulary.exampleEN: Her counterargument pointed out that closing the street could hurt local shops.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أشارت حجتها المضادة إلى أن إغلاق الشارع قد يضر المتاجر المحلية.

vocabulary.arabic: يُقِرّ بالنقطة / يوافق على جانب من الحق
vocabulary.definition: to accept that an opponent has a valid point, while keeping your main argument
vocabulary.exampleEN: I concede the point about parking, but I still believe the pedestrian zone will improve safety.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أقُرّ بمسألة مواقف السيارات، لكنني أعتقد أن المنطقة المخصصة للمشاة ستُحسّن السلامة.

vocabulary.definition: to consider all the evidence before making a decision
vocabulary.exampleEN: Before deciding, the council must weigh the evidence from the traffic study and the businesses.
vocabulary.exampleAR: قبل اتخاذ القرار يجب على المجلس أن يقيّم الأدلة من دراسة المرور والمتاجر.

vocabulary.definition: to give reasons or proof that make an assertion more believable
vocabulary.exampleEN: Local data supports the claim that pollution levels drop when cars are restricted.
vocabulary.exampleAR: تدعم البيانات المحلية الادعاء بأن مستويات التلوث تنخفض عند تقييد السيارات.

vocabulary.definition: to reduce people's trust in someone or something, often by showing mistakes or bias
vocabulary.exampleEN: Using an unreliable survey could undermine the credibility of the proposal.
vocabulary.exampleAR: قد يضعف استخدام استبيان غير موثوق مصداقية الاقتراح.

vocabulary.definition: a person, organisation, or document known to provide accurate information
vocabulary.exampleEN: The traffic report from the university is a reliable source we can use.
vocabulary.exampleAR: تقرير المرور من الجامعة مصدر موثوق يمكننا استخدامه.

vocabulary.arabic: يتعامل مع المخاوف / يجيب على المخاوف
vocabulary.definition: to acknowledge and offer a response to people's worries
vocabulary.exampleEN: The plan should address concerns about deliveries to shops during the day.
vocabulary.exampleAR: يجب أن يتعامل الخطة مع المخاوف بشأن التوصيل إلى المتاجر أثناء النهار.

vocabulary.definition: showing unfair preference for or against something; not objective
vocabulary.exampleEN: The newspaper article seemed biased because it only quoted supporters.
vocabulary.exampleAR: بدا مقال الصحيفة متحيزًا لأنه اقتبس فقط من المؤيدين.

vocabulary.definition: used to introduce a personal opinion politely
vocabulary.exampleEN: In my view, a compromise that keeps some parking would work best.
vocabulary.exampleAR: في رأيي، التسوية التي تحتفظ ببعض مواقف السيارات ستكون الأفضل.

vocabulary.arabic: يلعب دور المحاور للجدل / يناقش الفكرة ليرى نقاط الضعف
vocabulary.definition: to argue the opposite position to test the strength of an argument
vocabulary.exampleEN: I'll play devil’s advocate and ask if emergency vehicles can still pass quickly.
vocabulary.exampleAR: سأقوم بدور المناقض وأسأل إن كانت المركبات الطارئة لا تزال قادرة على العبور بسرعة.

grammar.topic: structured argument and concession
grammar.concept: Use clear organisation (position, reasons + evidence, concession, reply, conclusion) and linking phrases to show concession (e.g., 'I accept that...', 'although', 'however', 'nevertheless'). A concession recognises a valid point of the other side but then explains why your position still stands.
grammar.arabicComparison: في العربية، قد تعبِّر عن الاتفاق الجزئي بعبارات مثل 'أوافق على أن...' ثم تتبعها تفسيرًا. نفس الفكرة هنا: اعترف بنقطة معقولة ثم أعطِ سببًا يبقى موقفك.
grammar.structure: Intro (position). Reason 1 + evidence. Reason 2 + evidence. Concession (e.g., 'I accept that X') + short counter (e.g., 'however', 'nevertheless'). Conclusion / recommendation.
grammar.commonError: Either ignoring the opposing view or making a concession without a clear follow-up reply. Also, using weak evidence (opinions only) instead of specific examples or data.
grammar.exampleEN: I support the pedestrian zone because it will reduce accidents and pollution. I accept that parking for customers will be harder; however, the council could add short-term parking nearby to help shops.
grammar.exampleAR: أدعم منطقة المشاة لأنها ستقلل الحوادث والتلوث. أقرّ بأن مواقف السيارات للزبائن ستكون أصعب؛ ومع ذلك، يمكن للمجلس إضافة مواقف قصيرة المدة قريبة لمساعدة المتاجر.

readingBrief: Read an original 250–350-word opinion article for the local community newsletter about a proposed traffic plan to pedestrianise part of the high street. The piece will include: a clear position for or against the plan, two supporting reasons each with one piece of evidence (e.g., local data, expert comment, business feedback), one reasonable counterargument from opponents, and a short concession and reply. Focus: identify claims, the type and strength of evidence, concession language, and recommended solutions.
writingPrompt: Write a 140–180-word letter to the town council (audience: council members and community readers) giving your balanced opinion on the proposed traffic scheme. Purpose: present your position, give two reasons with evidence or examples, acknowledge one sensible objection (concession) and respond briefly, and end with a clear recommendation. Success criteria: organise your letter with a short introduction, two body paragraphs (reason + evidence each), one concession paragraph with a reply, and a concluding recommendation; keep a polite, balanced tone. Use at least two target chunks from this lesson (for example, 'present evidence' or 'concede the point').

title: The next chapter

outcome.canDo: I can reflect on past experiences, explain my next steps and make realistic plans using a range of future forms and linking language.
outcome.canDoArabic: أَستطيع التأمّل في تجاربي السابقة وشرح خطواتي التالية ووضع خطط واقعية باستخدام أشكال الأزمنة المستقبلية وعبارات الربط.
outcome.scenario: You are writing an email to a close friend about the end of one stage in your life (job, course, relationship, etc.) and your practical plans for the next chapter. You need to explain what changed, evaluate options, and describe clear next steps.
outcome.scenarioArabic: تكتب رسالة إلكترونية إلى صديق مقرب عن نهاية مرحلة في حياتك (وظيفة، دورة، علاقة، إلخ) وخططك العملية للفصل التالي. تحتاج إلى شرح ما تغيّر، تقييم الخيارات، ووصف خطوات واضحة تالية.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: List three important experiences from the last two years and for each write one short sentence about what you learned and one short sentence about one small change you want to make next.
retrieval.purpose: Activate A2-level vocabulary on experiences and simple plans, and prepare learners to combine those ideas into a connected B1 narrative.

retrieval.language: Arabic
retrieval.prompt: اكتب خدمتين أو خدمات استخدمتهما (مثل دورة، بنك، تدريب) وصِف ما أعجبك وما لم يعجبك في جملة واحدة لكل خدمة، ثم اذكر خطة واحدة لتحسين تجربتك مع كل خدمة.
retrieval.purpose: Repurpose A2 language about services and preferences into a short evaluative task that supports analysis and planning at B1.

retrieval.language: English
retrieval.prompt: Think of a habit or routine you changed. Note when it changed, why you changed it (your opinion), and two specific steps you will take next to keep improving.
retrieval.purpose: Reuse A2 items (opinions, change, plans) and push learners to produce a sequenced plan and a qualified opinion for B1-level output.

network.learningNote: At B1 learners need to move from listing experiences and simple plans to telling a connected story: link past events to future choices. Use a mix of past tenses, present perfect and several future forms plus discourse markers (e.g. 'looking back', 'moving forward'). Teach realistic, specific steps rather than vague intentions.
network.learningNoteArabic: في مستوى B1 يحتاج المتعلّمون للانتقال من تعداد التجارب والخطط البسيطة إلى سرد مترابط: اربط الأحداث السابقة بالخيارات المستقبلية. استخدم مزيجاً من أزمنة الماضي، المضارع التام، وأشكال المستقبل مع أدوات الربط (مثل «بالنظر إلى الوراء»، «في المضي قدماً»). علّم خطوات واقعية ومحددة بدلاً من نوايا غامضة.

wordFamilies.note: Use both noun and verb; 'planning' is useful for ongoing arrangements.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: 'plan' تُستخدم كاسم وفعل؛ 'planning' مناسبة للخطط المستمرة.

wordFamilies.note: Reflection language helps compare past and future choices.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: لغة التأمّل تساعد على مقارنة الخيارات السابقة والمستقبلية.

wordFamilies.note: Balance honest reflection with confident language to sound realistic.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: وازن بين التأمّل الصادق ولغة الثقة لتبدو واقعياً.

vocabulary.definition: to review and evaluate past events or progress
vocabulary.exampleEN: Before moving on to the next chapter, take stock of what you’ve learned.
vocabulary.exampleAR: قبل الانتقال إلى الفصل التالي، قُم بتقييم ما تعلمته.

vocabulary.arabic: يعبر إلى فصل جديد / يبدأ صفحة جديدة
vocabulary.definition: to leave a past situation and begin something different
vocabulary.exampleEN: After the course finished, she decided it was time to turn the page.
vocabulary.exampleAR: بعد انتهاء الدورة قررت أنها حان الوقت لبدء فصل جديد.

vocabulary.definition: to begin a new period in life with different priorities or activities
vocabulary.exampleEN: He's moving cities to start a new chapter in his career.
vocabulary.exampleAR: سينتقل إلى مدينة أخرى ليبدأ فصلاً جديدًا في مسيرته المهنية.

vocabulary.definition: to decide important stages that show progress toward a longer-term plan
vocabulary.exampleEN: She identified milestones for her training so she could track improvement.
vocabulary.exampleAR: حددت معالم رئيسية لتدريبها حتى تتمكن من تتبع التحسّن.

vocabulary.definition: a detailed proposal for doing or achieving something; to decide on actions in advance
vocabulary.exampleEN: My plan is to study part-time and take one course at a time.
vocabulary.exampleAR: خَطّتي أن أدرس بدوام جزئي وآخذ دورة واحدة في كل مرة.

vocabulary.definition: the process of making plans for something
vocabulary.exampleEN: Careful planning helped her balance work and family.
vocabulary.exampleAR: ساعدها التخطيط الدقيق على موازنة العمل والعائلة.

vocabulary.definition: to think carefully about something, especially your feelings or behaviour
vocabulary.exampleEN: He paused to reflect on what had gone well and what had not.
vocabulary.exampleAR: توقف ليتأمل فيما سار على ما يرام وما لم ينجح.

vocabulary.definition: serious thought about past events, decisions or experiences
vocabulary.exampleEN: Her reflection showed that she needed more practical training.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أظهر تأملُها أنها بحاجة إلى تدريب عملي أكثر.

vocabulary.definition: feeling sure about your own ability or plan
vocabulary.exampleEN: I'm confident I can manage this new role with support.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أنا واثق أني أستطيع إدارة هذا الدور الجديد بمساعدة.

vocabulary.definition: the feeling or belief that you can do something well

vocabulary.exampleAR: استغرق اكتساب الثقة وقتًا لكن الانتصارات الصغيرة ساعدت كثيرًا.

vocabulary.definition: to consider the advantages and disadvantages of different choices
vocabulary.exampleEN: Before deciding, she weighed up the options with a friend.
vocabulary.exampleAR: قبل اتخاذ القرار وزنّت الخيارات مع صديقة.

vocabulary.definition: to do a specific, useful action that moves you towards a goal
vocabulary.exampleEN: A practical step was booking a short course to build skills.
vocabulary.exampleAR: كانت خطوة عملية حجز دورة قصيرة لبناء المهارات.

grammar.topic: Integrated B1 review and future perspective
grammar.arabicName: مراجعة متكاملة للمستوى B1 ومنظور المستقبل
grammar.concept: Review how to describe past events briefly and link them to concrete future plans. Integrate past simple, present perfect, present continuous for future arrangements, 'going to' for intentions and 'will' for predictions or offers. Use sequencing and linking language (e.g. 'looking back', 'as a result', 'next', 'moving forward').
grammar.arabicComparison: بالعربية نستخدم سـ/سوف للمستقبل أو المضارع مع ظرف للمستقبل؛ في الإنجليزية هناك أكثر من شكل: 'going to' للنوايا، المضارع المستمر للترتيبات، و 'will' للتنبؤات والوعود. أيضاً تُستخدم أزمنة الماضي بصورة مختلفة لوصف الخبرات.
grammar.structure: Past: I worked / I have worked. Future plans: I'm going to / I'm + -ing (next week) / I will. Linking: Looking back, ... As a result, ... Next, ...
grammar.commonError: Mixing 'going to' and 'will' without thinking about intention vs prediction (e.g. saying 'I will study tonight' when you already arranged it). Also underuse of linking phrases when telling a connected story.
grammar.exampleEN: Looking back, I worked in retail for three years and learned how to manage customers. Next, I'm going to take a short course in digital marketing and I will apply for part-time roles to gain experience.
grammar.exampleAR: بالنظر إلى الوراء، عملت في التجزئة لمدة ثلاث سنوات وتعلمت كيفية إدارة العملاء. التالي أنني سأخذ دورة قصيرة في التسويق الرقمي وسأتقدم لوظائف بدوام جزئي لاكتساب الخبرة.

readingBrief: An original 250–350-word first-person interview with a mid-career professional who explains the end of a long role, what they learned, how they weighed up new options, and the three practical steps they will take next. Expect past simple and present perfect to describe experience, discourse markers ('looking back', 'as a result', 'moving forward') and several future expressions ('going to', present continuous for arrangements, and 'will'). The piece should be conversational but organised (intro, reflection, decision, next steps).
writingPrompt: Write an email (140–180 words) to a close friend describing your 'next chapter'. Purpose: briefly reflect on one important experience you had, explain the decision you made, and list two practical steps you will take next. Audience: a close friend who knows you well. Success criteria: organise your email into three short paragraphs (reflection, decision, next steps), keep an honest but confident tone, and use at least two different future expressions (for example 'going to' and present continuous) to describe your plans.

grammar.topic: Discourse markers for sequence and contrast
grammar.concept: This B1 pattern helps you connect travel and change ideas so the listener or reader can follow your meaning.

grammar.structure: Discourse markers for sequence and contrast: choose the form, add the idea, then check the time and relationship between clauses.
grammar.commonError: Using two short sentences when the context needs one connected idea, or choosing a connector that changes the intended relationship.
grammar.exampleEN: Although the situation was difficult, we made a practical decision because we had enough information.
grammar.exampleAR: مع أن الموقف كان صعباً، اتخذنا قراراً عملياً لأن لدينا معلومات كافية.

grammar.topic: Discourse markers for sequence and contrast

grammar.structure: Discourse markers for sequence and contrast: choose the form, add the idea, then check the time and relationship between clauses.
